definition_zh: 中世纪的；中世纪风格的；中世纪式的（野蛮、落后）；中世纪的人
definition_en: belonging to the Middle Ages, or resembling the period in style, and by extension crude or backward
core_image: 一张泛黄的羊皮纸上画着带雉堞的城墙、修士与骑士，边角发脆，墨色已经被时间咬出小洞
scene: 修道院的抄经房里，烛光下摊着羊皮卷，抄写者正一个字母一个字母地描。A medieval scribe copied the chronicle by candlelight, one letter at a time.
sceneCN: 这里 medieval 指「属于中世纪时期的」（第 1 个义项：时间上属中世纪）；句意为一位中世纪的抄写员借烛光逐字母抄录编年史。场景物件：羊皮卷、烛台、羽毛笔、窗洞；对应第 1 个义项。

中世纪的人；(复数)中世纪的文物与研究

senses.title: Belonging to the Middle Ages
senses.definition: dating from or existing in the period between classical antiquity and the Renaissance
senses.definitionCN: 属于古典时代与文艺复兴之间那段时期的
senses.example: A medieval scribe copied the chronicle by candlelight.
senses.exampleCN: 一位中世纪的抄写员借烛光抄录编年史。
senses.why: the adjective simply dates a thing by placing it between the ancient and the modern, which is what medium aevum means.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只按「夹在古代与现代之间」给事物定年，而 medium aevum 正是此意。

senses.title: Typical of the period's culture
senses.titleCN: 具有中世纪文化特征的
senses.definition: showing the customs, faith, dress or building habits of that period
senses.definitionCN: 表现出那一时期的习俗、信仰、衣着或营造方式
senses.example: The church keeps a medieval nave, a medieval rood screen and a medieval bell.
senses.exampleCN: 这座教堂保有中世纪的中殿、圣像屏与铜钟。
senses.why: culture, not the calendar, is being named here: the shape of an arch or a rite identifies the age.
senses.whyCN: 这里说的是文化而非日历：拱券的形状或一种仪式就标出了年代。

senses.title: Revived in medieval style
senses.definition: made in deliberate imitation of medieval forms by a later age
senses.definitionCN: 由后世刻意模仿中世纪形式而制作的
senses.example: Victorian architects added a medieval tower to a plain Georgian church.
senses.exampleCN: 维多利亚时代的建筑师给一座朴素的乔治式教堂加上了中世纪风格的塔楼。
senses.why: once the period was safely past, copying it became a style, and the adjective moved from origin to imitation.
senses.whyCN: 当那段时期安全地过去，模仿它就成了一种风格，形容词也从「出自当时」变成「仿其形」。

senses.title: Harsh and brutal, as imagined of the age
senses.definition: cruel or primitive in a way associated in popular memory with that period
senses.definitionCN: 以一种大众记忆中所认为的中世纪方式残酷、原始
senses.example: The sentence was medieval in its plainness: a fine, a whip and a wall.
senses.exampleCN: 那判决残酷得直白：罚金、鞭子与一堵墙。
senses.why: popular history reduced a long period to a single mood, and the adjective carried that mood into metaphors.
senses.whyCN: 通俗历史把漫长的时期压缩成一种情绪，形容词便把这情绪带进比喻。

senses.title: Backward or outdated
senses.definition: used of attitudes or systems thought to belong to a less advanced age
senses.definitionCN: 指被认为属于较低发展阶段的态度或制度
senses.example: The company's medieval attitude to leave kept good staff away.
senses.exampleCN: 公司那套中世纪式的休假态度把好员工挡在门外。
senses.why: the same historical distance now measures progress: to be medieval is to be behind, not merely old.
senses.whyCN: 同一种历史距离此时用来衡量进步：说人「中世纪」就是说他落后，而不只是旧。

senses.title: A person who lived in the period
senses.definition: a person living in the Middle Ages, used mostly in histories and in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 生活在那一时期的人，多用于历史叙述与复数形式
senses.example: The medievals counted years from creation, not from a birth in Bethlehem.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪人从创世而非从伯利恒的那次降生起算年份。
senses.why: the noun is simply the adjective standing alone, a common English shortcut for 'people of that time'.
senses.whyCN: 名词只是形容词独立使用，是英语里表示「那个时代的人」的常见省略。

senses.title: Objects or works of the period
senses.definition: collected medieval artefacts or texts, used in the plural by dealers and scholars
senses.definitionCN: 旧物商与学者用来指收集起来的中世纪器物或文本，多用复数
senses.example: The auction grouped the medievals with the early printed books.
senses.exampleCN: 拍卖行把中世纪的器物与早期印本归在一起。
senses.why: specialist speech turns the adjective into a noun for the things themselves, so a category label becomes a shelf label.
senses.whyCN: 专业行话把形容词转成指物件本身的名词，于是分类标签变成了货架标签。

senses.title: Of medieval Latin or manuscript tradition
senses.titleCN: 中世纪拉丁语与手抄传统的
senses.definition: used of the Latin, script or textual tradition of the period, as distinct from classical forms
senses.definitionCN: 指那一时期的拉丁语、字体或文本传统，以区别于古典形式
senses.example: The glossary lists medieval Latin spellings beside classical ones.
senses.exampleCN: 这部词表把中世纪拉丁拼法列在古典拼法旁边。
senses.why: scholars needed a term for the period's own written language, and the adjective was narrowed onto the manuscript world.
senses.whyCN: 学者需要为那一时期自身的书面语命名，形容词便收窄到手稿世界。

intro.en: Medieval goes back to Modern Latin medium aevum 'middle age', a label invented by scholars to name the gap between antiquity and their own day.
intro.cn: medieval 可追到近代拉丁 medium aevum「中间的时代」，这是学者为古代与自身时代之间的空档所造的标签。

items.en: Medium aevum 'middle age' was coined by learned writers in the seventeenth century as a neutral dividing label.
items.cn: medium aevum「中间的时代」由 17 世纪的学者造出，用作中性的分段标签。

items.en: Medius 'middle' is an old Italic adjective, and aevum 'age, lifetime' supplies the time word; the deeper origin of aevum is not settled.
items.cn: medius「中间」是古老的意大利语族形容词，aevum「年纪、一生」提供时间义；aevum 更深来源并无定论。

items.en: English took the Modern Latin adjective mediaevalis in the early nineteenth century and spelled it mediaeval.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪初借入近代拉丁形容词 mediaevalis，拼作 mediaeval。

items.en: Twentieth-century printers dropped the digraph, so medieval is now standard while mediaeval survives in older titles.
items.cn: 20 世纪的印刷习惯去掉了二合元音，medieval 成为标准，mediaeval 只留在旧书名里。

items.en: The word also acquired a tone: to call something medieval can mean picturesque, superstitious or simply brutal.
items.cn: 这个词还带上语调：说某物「中世纪的」可以指如画、迷信，也可以指纯粹野蛮。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact year of the Latin coinage is undocumented, and the earliest English use is dated loosely to the 1810s to 1820s.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：拉丁造词的确切年份无文献可查，英语最早用例只能约略定在 19 世纪一十至二十年代。

note.en: Group one holds the spellings and near neighbours of the same word; group two holds period words that are often substituted for it.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词的拼写变体与形近词；第二组是常被拿来替换它的分期词。

entries.definition: The pre-twentieth-century spelling of the same adjective, still used in reprints of old scholarship.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个形容词在 20 世纪前的拼法，仍见于旧学术著作的重印本。

entries.definition: The noun for the cult or imitation of medieval forms, so it names a later taste rather than a date.
entries.definitionCN: 指对中世纪形式的迷恋或模仿，因此是后世的趣味，而非一个年代。

entries.definition: A person who studies the period; the ending marks a person, not a time.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究那一时期的学者；词尾标出的是人，不是时间。

entries.definition: Built from middle and age but means 'neither young nor old' about a person, with no historical reference.
entries.definitionCN: 同样由 middle 与 age 构成，却指人「中年」，与历史分期无关。

entries.definition: Covers the Greek and Roman world and earlier; medieval begins where ancient ends.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖希腊罗马世界及更早时期；medieval 从 ancient 结束处开始。

entries.tag: the high culture of greece and rome
entries.definition: Names the art and learning held up as models, which medieval culture was later said to have lost.
entries.definitionCN: 指被奉为典范的希腊罗马艺术与学术，后世常说中世纪丢失了它们。

entries.definition: A narrower word for land and service relations, not for the whole period or its art.
entries.definitionCN: 较窄的词，指土地与服役关系，不指整个时期或其艺术。

entries.definition: The pointed-arch style within the period, and later a taste for the gloomy and wild.
entries.definitionCN: 指那一时期内的尖拱风格，后来也指对阴森狂野之趣的偏好。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin components, real spellings and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁成分、真实的拼写与现代同族词。

normal.en: medium aevum 'middle age': the period sits in the middle, between antiquity and the modern world.
normal.cn: medium aevum「中间的时代」：这一段夹在古代与现代之间。

normal.en: The same media- appears in medium, median and intermediate, all 'middle' words.
normal.cn: 同样的 media- 出现在 medium、median、intermediate，都是「中间」的词。

normal.en: Two spellings are current in older texts: medieval and mediaeval.
normal.cn: 旧文本里两种拼法都在用：medieval 与 mediaeval。

normal.en: The family runs medieval, medievalism, medievalist, medievalistic, medievalize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 medieval、medievalism、medievalist、medievalistic、medievalize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases date the word: medieval history, medieval Latin, medieval manuscript.
normal.cn: 固定搭配替它定位：中世纪史、中世纪拉丁语、中世纪手稿。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with one long square greyed out between two bright ones.
abstract.cn: 想象一张日历，两个明亮的格子之间有一长格被涂成灰色。

abstract.en: Picture a candle burning beside a page that curls at the corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛在旁燃烧，纸页的一角卷了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a stone arch that is round below and pointed above.
abstract.cn: 想象一座石拱，下面圆、上面尖。

examples.en: Medieval walls still ring the old town, though the gates are gone.
examples.cn: 中世纪的城墙仍围着老城，只是城门早已不存。

examples.en: The museum labels the piece medieval, though its date is disputed.
examples.cn: 博物馆把这件器物标为中世纪，尽管年代仍有争议。

examples.en: Critics called the punishment medieval and demanded a review.
examples.cn: 批评者称那项惩罚野蛮落后，要求复核。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「medi」听似「没底」，中间一段没底的年月 → 夹在古代与近代之间的中世纪

root: 近代拉丁 medium aevum「中间的时代」= medius「中间」+ aevum「年纪、一生」；经近代拉丁形容词 mediaevalis 进入英语。aevum 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a date to a mood: a period, its culture, a later imitation of it, the cruelty and backwardness people read into it, and finally the people and manuscripts that carry the name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个年代走向一种情绪：先是时期，再是时期的文化，再是后世的仿制，再是人们读进去的野蛮与落后，最后是承载这个名字的人与手稿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brittle parchment page showing a battlemented wall, a monk and a knight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张发脆的羊皮纸，上面画着雉堞城墙、修士与骑士。

branches.en: DATE AND CULTURE: one sense places a thing in time, the other reads the period's habits from the thing itself.
branches.cn: 年代与文化：一个义项替事物定位在时间上，另一个从事物本身读出那一时期的习惯。

branches.en: REVIVAL: a later age copies the forms, and origin becomes imitation.
branches.cn: 复兴：后世复制其形制，于是「出自当时」变成「仿其形」。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT: the same distance that makes the period picturesque also makes it a byword for cruelty and backwardness.
branches.cn: 评判：同一种距离既让那时期显得如画，也让其成为野蛮与落后的代名词。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND OBJECTS: the adjective standing alone names the people of the period and, in trade talk, their artefacts.
branches.cn: 人与物：形容词独立使用指那一时期的人，在行话里也指其器物。

branches.en: MANUSCRIPT TRADITION: scholarship narrows the word onto the period's own Latin, script and texts.
branches.cn: 手稿传统：学术用法把它收窄到那一时期自身的拉丁语、字体与文本。

intro.en: Medieval is a Modern Latin phrase compressed into one English adjective, and its pieces also build other common words.
intro.cn: medieval 是把一个近代拉丁短语压缩成的一个英语形容词，它的各部分还构成别的常用词。

latinIntro.en: Latin medius 'middle' also yields medium, median and intermediate, while aevum 'age' appears in longevity and in aevum-based historical labels.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 medius「中间」还衍生 medium、median、intermediate；aevum「年纪」见于 longevity 及以 aevum 构成的历史标签。

items.example: The root places the period between two others.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把这一段放在另外两段之间。

items.example: The second element supplies the time span.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分提供时间跨度。

items.example: The suffix turns the phrase into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把短语变成形容词。

items.example: The medieval register is still legible.
items.exampleCN: 那本中世纪的登记簿仍可辨读。

items.meaning: the cult or study of medieval forms
items.example: Medievalism rebuilt the abbey in pointed arches.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪风用尖拱重建了这座修道院。

items.example: The medievalist read the charter aloud.
items.exampleCN: 这位中世纪学者把特许状读了出来。

items.meaning: in the manner of medieval scholarship
items.example: The essay has a medievalistic fondness for lineage.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章带着中世纪研究式的谱系癖。

items.example: The filmmaker medievalized the city with fake towers.
items.exampleCN: 制片人用假塔楼把这座城市中世纪化。

items.example: The mediaeval spelling survives in reprints.
items.exampleCN: mediaeval 这一旧拼法仍留在重印本里。

definition_zh: 媒介；手段；媒体；中等的；灵媒
definition_en: a channel or means that carries something between two sides; also the middle point of a scale, and a person who claims to speak with spirits
core_image: 一只手把碗端在身前正中，不高不低，左右都不偏
scene: 戏台上，老艺人把一只小碗端在胸前，碗里盛着半碗水，不多不少，正好让台下看清碗底的纹路。The old performer held the bowl at a medium height so that everyone in the yard could see the pattern inside.
sceneCN: 这里 medium 是「中等的、适中的高度」（第 3 个义项：处在两个极端之间）；句意为老艺人把碗端到中等的高度，好让院子里的人都看清碗里的花纹。

pos.zh: 媒介；手段；媒体；灵媒
中等的；适中的

derivatives.zh: medium 的复数形式，专指报纸、电视、网络等新闻传播机构
由 medium 与 sized 复合而成，义为「中等大小的」
由 medium 加表示身份状态的后缀 -ship 构成，义为「通灵的本领」

senses.title: A channel that carries something between two sides
senses.definition: something used to carry information, ideas or influence from one person or place to another
senses.definitionCN: 用来把信息、思想或影响从一方传到另一方的东西
senses.example: Speech was the first medium for passing stories down the generations.
senses.exampleCN: 口头讲述是把故事传给后代的第一种媒介。
senses.why: Latin medius means middle, and a medium literally sits in the middle, so the word starts from the gap it bridges rather than from the message it carries.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 medius 意为「中间的」，媒介就字面地待在中间，所以这个词的起点是它所连接的那道缝隙，而不是它运送的内容。

senses.title: Newspapers and broadcasters taken as one body
senses.definition: the press, television, radio and online outlets considered together as the channel that reaches the public
senses.definitionCN: 把报纸、电视、广播和网络平台合起来看，作为面向公众发声的渠道
senses.example: The story stayed out of the media for three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事在媒体上压了三个星期没有露面。
senses.why: Once the channel is owned by companies and staffed by editors, the plural media stops naming a means and starts naming an industry with its own habits and power.
senses.whyCN: 当渠道归公司所有、由编辑操持，复数 media 就不再指某种手段，而是指一个有自己的习惯与权力的行业。

senses.title: Halfway between two extremes
senses.definition: of a size, amount or degree that lies between the largest and the smallest
senses.definitionCN: 大小、数量或程度处在一个区间的中间，不在两端
senses.example: Ask for a medium cup if the strong one keeps you awake.
senses.exampleCN: 如果浓的那款让你睡不着，就要一杯中杯。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the plain picture of the Latin root: a mark in the middle of a scale, chosen because neither end suits the purpose.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义保留了拉丁词根最朴素的画面：刻度中间的那一格，因为两端都不合用才选它。

senses.title: A person who claims to hear the dead
senses.definition: someone who says that messages from the dead reach them and that they can pass replies back
senses.definitionCN: 自称能收到死者的讯息、并把回话带回去的人
senses.example: The medium said a visitor from the other side had sat in the empty chair.
senses.exampleCN: 那位灵媒说，有位来自另一边的访客曾坐在那把空椅子上。
senses.why: Here the person again occupies the middle, standing between the living and the dead as a go-between, which is why this sense keeps the plural mediums instead of media.
senses.whyCN: 这里的人又一次占据中间位置，夹在生者与死者之间充当传话者，所以这个义项复数用 mediums 而不是 media。

intro.en: Medium is Latin for middle. English first borrowed it as a noun for a carrier, then let the plural media grow into the press and kept mediums for spirit talkers and middle sizes.
intro.cn: medium 是拉丁语中表示「中间」的词。英语先把它借作名词指承载之物，之后复数 media 长成「媒体」，而 mediums 留给灵媒与中间尺码。

items.en: Medius was the everyday Latin adjective for middle, used of anything placed between two others.
items.cn: medius 是拉丁语里表示「中间的」常用形容词，凡夹在两者之间的事物都用它。

items.en: The neuter form medium named the middle point of a space and also an element that stood between two others.
items.cn: 中性形式 medium 指空间的中点，也指介于另外两者之间的要素。

items.en: The verb mediare meant to be in the middle or to split something in half, and it produced a family of words about standing between parties.
items.cn: 动词 mediare 意为居于中间或把东西分成两半，派生出一族表示「居间」的词。

items.en: English took medium for whatever carries something else, such as air carrying sound or a person carrying a message.
items.cn: 英语借 medium 指承载他物的东西，例如传声的空气，或替人带话的信使。

items.en: The plural media came to mean the news industry, while mediums stayed with people who contact spirits; both plurals also name sizes that fall between small and large.
items.cn: 复数 media 逐渐指新闻业，mediums 则留给与亡灵沟通的人；两种复数也都用来指介于大小之间的尺码。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin root for middle through several English words; the near-meaning group gathers words for a means of passing something on.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「中间」的拉丁词根串起几个英语词；近义组收表示「传递某物的手段」的词。

entries.definition: To stand between two sides and help them settle a dispute.
entries.definitionCN: 站在两方之间，帮他们解决争端。

entries.definition: Belonging to the Middle Ages, the period between ancient and modern times.
entries.definitionCN: 属于中世纪的，即古代与近代之间的时期。

entries.definition: Happening at once, with nothing standing in between.
entries.definitionCN: 立刻发生的，中间没有间隔。

entries.definition: Only middling in quality, neither good nor bad.
entries.definitionCN: 质量平平的，既不好也不坏。

entries.definition: A method or thing used to get a result.
entries.definitionCN: 用来达到结果的方法或东西。

entries.definition: A route or system through which something is passed on.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物传出去的途径或系统。

entries.definition: Something that carries an idea or a message, as well as a machine that carries people.
entries.definitionCN: 既指载人的交通工具，也指承载思想或讯息的东西。

entries.definition: The power or means by which something is done.
entries.definitionCN: 做成某事所凭借的力量或手段。

normalIntro.en: The whole family circles one Latin idea, the middle, and the word keeps that position in every sense it takes on.
normalIntro.cn: 整族词都绕着拉丁语的一个意思——「中间」——打转，这个词每多一个义项，也仍然站在那个位置上。

normal.en: Medius is Latin for middle, so a medium is literally what sits in the middle between two sides.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 medius 意为中间，所以 medium 字面上就是夹在两方中间的那个东西。

normal.en: Media is the plural used for news outlets, which is why the word often appears with a plural verb in that sense.
normal.cn: media 是用于新闻机构的复数形式，所以这个义项常与复数动词连用。

normal.en: A medium shirt sits on the middle hook, between the small and the large, and the adjective follows the same picture.
normal.cn: 中号衬衫挂在中间那只钩子上，夹在小号与大号之间，形容词义用的是同一幅画面。

normal.en: Mediums, not media, is the plural for spirit talkers, because those people stand between two worlds rather than between two sizes.
normal.cn: 灵媒的复数是 mediums 而不是 media，因为这些人站在两个世界之间，而不是两个尺码之间。

normal.en: Mediocre comes from the same middle root and means only middling, a useful reminder that middle can also mean unremarkable.
normal.cn: mediocre 出自同一表示「中间」的词根，意为平平无奇，正好提醒人：中间也可以指不出众。

abstract.en: Every medium is a bridge, and a bridge is only noticed when it fails to carry anything across.
abstract.cn: 每个媒介都是一座桥，而桥只有在运不过东西时才会被人注意到。

abstract.en: A word for the middle ends up naming the press, the spirits and the middle shelf, because all three are places where two sides meet.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「中间」的词最后指媒体、亡灵与中间货架，因为这三者都是两方相遇的地方。

abstract.en: To choose a medium is to accept that the shape of the channel quietly shapes what travels through it.
abstract.cn: 选择一种媒介，就等于承认渠道的形状会悄悄塑造从中经过的东西。

examples.en: Air is the medium that carries a voice across a room.
examples.cn: 空气是把声音送过房间的媒介。

examples.en: The news media covered the election through the night.
examples.cn: 新闻媒体整夜报道这场选举。

examples.en: This jacket comes in small, medium and large.
examples.cn: 这件外套有小号、中号和大号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米迪姆」——把米分成两半，正好落在中间；记住 medium 是中间、媒介。

root: 拉丁语 medius（中间的）→ 中性名词 medium（中点、居间之物）；复数 media 后专指媒体，mediums 则保留灵媒义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the middle position. From it grow the carrier between two sides, the press that owns the carriers, the middle of a scale, and the person who stands between the living and the dead.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「中间的位置」。由此长出两方之间的承载物、拥有这些渠道的媒体、刻度上的中间一格，以及站在生者与死者之间的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl held at the exact middle of the body, level with the chest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只碗端在身体正中，与胸口齐平。

branches.en: a messenger handing a letter across a river
branches.cn: 信使在河边把信递到对岸

branches.en: an editor deciding which faces appear on the front page
branches.cn: 编辑决定谁的脸能上头版

branches.en: a shirt hanging on the middle hook of a rack
branches.cn: 衣架中间那只钩子上的一件衬衫

branches.en: a dim room where an unfamiliar voice answers
branches.cn: 昏暗房间里有个陌生的声音回应

branches.en: a scale whose middle mark is the safest choice
branches.cn: 刻度尺上中间那一格最稳妥

senses.definition: To come together with someone by chance or by plan
senses.definitionCN: 与某人相遇
senses.example: I met my teacher on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 我在回家路上遇到了老师。
senses.why: Old English metan meant to come upon; a chance meeting and an arranged one share the same picture of two paths crossing.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 metan 意为碰见；偶遇与约见都共享两条路交叉的同一画面。

senses.definitionCN: 达到要求或满足需要

senses.whyCN: 两样东西相遇也可指需求与供给恰好碰头，于是 meet 有了满足之义。

definition_zh: 融化；熔化；消散；心软
definition_en: to change from a solid into a liquid under heat, and, by extension, to fade away or to lose hardness of feeling
core_image: 一小块黄油落在烧热的铁锅上，边缘先塌下去，摊成一圈亮亮的油
scene: 厨房里，一小块黄油落进烧热的铁锅，边缘先塌下去，转眼摊成一圈亮亮的油。The last of the snow began to melt on the sunny side of the roof.
sceneCN: 这里 melt 是「融化、化开」（第 1 个义项：固体受热变成液体）；句意为屋顶向阳那一面的残雪开始化开。

pos.zh: 融化；熔化；消散；心软
熔化后的食物；加奶酪的烤三明治

derivatives.zh: melt 的古老分词形式，专指高温下熔化的金属或岩石
由 melt 加 -ing 构成，义为「正在融化的」，也形容语气温柔
由 melt 与 down 复合而成，义为「熔毁」，也指体系或情绪的崩溃

senses.title: To turn from solid into liquid under heat
senses.definition: to change from a solid state into a liquid one, usually because heat reaches it
senses.definitionCN: 在热量作用下从固态变成液态
senses.example: The ice on the pond melted before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘上的冰不到中午就化了。
senses.why: Old English meltan described a solid giving up its shape to warmth, so the physical change is the body of the word and every other sense borrows from it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 meltan 说的是固体在温度面前交出形状，所以这个物理变化是词的身骨，其余义项都从它借力。

senses.title: To liquefy metal for casting
senses.definition: to heat metal until it flows so that it can be poured into a mould
senses.definitionCN: 把金属加热到能流动，好倒进模具里成型
senses.example: The smith melted the old coins and cast them into a bell.
senses.exampleCN: 铁匠把旧钱币熔化，铸成了一口钟。
senses.why: Metal needs a heat far beyond what butter or snow can take, so this sense narrows the same change to the workshop and the foundry.
senses.whyCN: 金属承受的热远超过黄油或雪，所以这个义项把同一种变化收窄到作坊与铸炉之中。

senses.title: To fade until nothing is left
senses.definition: to grow weaker and then vanish, as a crowd, a sound or a feeling does
senses.definitionCN: 像人群、声音或情绪那样越来越弱，直到不见
senses.example: The anger in her voice melted away once she saw the broken window.
senses.exampleCN: 她一看到碎掉的窗子，声音里的火气就散掉了。
senses.why: A melting thing loses its outline and spreads into what surrounds it, which is just what a crowd or a mood does when it stops having a shape you can point at.
senses.whyCN: 融化的东西失去轮廓、摊进四周，人群或情绪不再是一个能指认的形状时，做的正是这件事。

senses.title: To lose hardness of feeling
senses.definition: to stop being cold or firm in attitude and become gentle or sympathetic
senses.definitionCN: 态度不再冷硬，转为温和、体谅
senses.example: Her heart melted when the boy handed her the crumpled flower.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩把那朵揉皱的花递给她时，她的心一下就软了。
senses.why: Wax and ice go soft when warmth reaches them, and English uses that same softening of matter for a person whose coldness suddenly gives way.
senses.whyCN: 蜡和冰遇到温度就变软，英语便用物质同样的软化来形容一个人忽然放下冷硬。

intro.en: Melt goes back to an Old English verb for becoming liquid, and it has stayed close to that bodily picture ever since. No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
intro.cn: melt 可上溯到古英语中表示「变成液体」的动词，此后一直紧贴那幅身体性的画面。这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.en: A reconstructed root often written meldh- is thought to have meant to soften or give way, but its exact shape is not certain.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个写作 meldh- 的构拟词根表示「变软、塌陷」，但确切形式并不确定。

items.en: The reconstructed verb meltanan carried the same idea into the Germanic languages, and its modern relatives still mean to melt.
items.cn: 构拟的动词 meltanan 把同一个意思带进日耳曼语族，它在现代各语言中的同族词仍表示「融化」。

items.en: Old English meltan meant to become liquid and could also describe a body or a thing wasting away.
items.cn: 古英语 meltan 意为变成液体，也可形容身体或物件渐渐消蚀。

items.en: Middle English kept melt for the physical change and began to use it for hard feelings that loosen.
items.cn: 中古英语的 melt 既保留物理变化，也开始用来指硬心肠的松动。

items.en: Modern English adds the noun melt, a dish topped with melted cheese, and keeps the figurative senses of fading and softening.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了名词 melt，指淋了熔化奶酪的热食，并保留「消散」与「心软」的比喻义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds forms and compounds built on the melting verb; the near-meaning group holds other words for turning soft or liquid, and for fading away.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在「融化」这个动词上的形式与复合词；近义组收其他表示变软、变液体以及消失的词。

entries.definition: Made liquid by great heat, said of metal, rock or glass.
entries.definitionCN: 被高温熔成液态的，多形容金属、岩石或玻璃。

entries.definition: In the process of becoming liquid, or soft enough to move someone.
entries.definitionCN: 正在化成液体的，也形容软到能打动人的。

entries.definition: A serious failure in which a core overheats, or any total collapse.
entries.definitionCN: 堆芯过热造成的严重事故，也指彻底的崩溃。

entries.definition: Grain that has been soaked and dried for brewing; it only looks like melt and comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 泡过再烘干的酿酒谷物；只是拼写与 melt 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To become soft or liquid again after being frozen.
entries.definitionCN: 冰冻之后重新变软、化开。

entries.definition: To be absorbed into a liquid and lose separate form.
entries.definitionCN: 被液体吸收而失去独立的形态。

entries.definition: To make or become liquid, used mostly in technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 使变成液体，多用于技术性文字。

entries.definition: To make something less hard, or less severe in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变软，或使态度不那么严厉。

normalIntro.en: The word is native English, and its forms split between the ordinary past and an older participle kept for hot metal.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本土词，它的各种形式分成了普通的过去式，以及专门留给高温金属的古老分词。

normal.en: Old English meltan already meant to become liquid, so the modern verb has barely moved in meaning.
normal.cn: 古英语 meltan 本来就表示变成液体，现代动词的意思几乎没有挪动。

normal.en: Melted serves as both past tense and past participle, while molten is the older participle that survived only for metal and rock.
normal.cn: melted 同时充当过去式与过去分词，molten 是只留给金属与岩石的古老分词。

normal.en: Melt down adds a downward particle and means to destroy something by melting it, which is why a reactor accident became a meltdown.
normal.cn: melt down 加了一个向下的虚词，意为把东西熔掉毁掉，反应堆事故因此被称为 meltdown。

normal.en: Melt in the mouth describes food so soft that the teeth are hardly needed.
normal.cn: melt in the mouth 形容食物软到几乎不用牙齿。

normal.en: Melt away uses away to show a shape thinning out until nothing remains to see.
normal.cn: melt away 用 away 表示轮廓一点点变淡，直到什么都看不见。

abstract.en: Anything that melts teaches the same lesson: hardness is only a temporary arrangement of warmth.
abstract.cn: 凡是能融化的东西都在讲同一件事：坚硬只是温度暂时给的一种排列。

abstract.en: A crowd melting away and a temper melting away share one picture, a shape that stops holding itself together.
abstract.cn: 人群散去和火气散去共用一幅画面——一个不再撑住自己的形状。

abstract.en: The word has no grand origin story, only a plain domestic change, and that plainness is why it works so well as a metaphor.
abstract.cn: 这个词没有宏大的来历，只有厨房里一个平常的变化，而正因为平常，它才这么好用作比喻。

examples.en: The snow melted as soon as the sun came out.
examples.cn: 太阳一出来，雪就化了。

examples.en: He melted the wax and used it to seal the letter.
examples.cn: 他把蜡化开，用来封住那封信。

examples.en: Her anger slowly melted away during the walk home.
examples.cn: 回家的路上，她的火气慢慢散掉了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卖它」——东西热到化掉，只好卖它换钱？记住 melt 是融化。

root: 古英语 meltan（变成液体），源自日耳曼语 meltanan，可上溯到构拟词根 meldh-（变软、塌陷）；无可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a solid losing its shape to heat. One branch stays literal and industrial, while the others follow the same loss of shape into fading and tenderness.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是固体在热中失去形状。一条分支留在字面与工业里，其余分支沿着同样的「失去形状」走向消散与温柔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pat of butter collapsing at the edge of a hot pan.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小块黄油在热锅边缘塌下去。

branches.en: butter sliding down the side of a hot pan
branches.cn: 黄油顺着热锅边滑下去

branches.en: sparks and a crucible in a foundry
branches.cn: 铸炉里的火星与坩埚

branches.en: a crowd thinning until the square is empty
branches.cn: 人群一点点散尽，广场空了

branches.en: a hand going limp around a flower
branches.cn: 握着花的手慢慢松开

branches.en: a snowman losing its edges in the sun
branches.cn: 雪人在太阳下一点点失去棱角

intro.en: The word is a native verb with Germanic ancestry, and its shape is held by old endings that mark tense, an old participle and a downward particle.
intro.cn: 这个词是带日耳曼血统的本土动词，它的形态由标记时态的古老词尾、一个古老分词和一个向下的虚词共同撑起。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，它的同族词都在日耳曼语族里。

definition_zh: 成员；会员；成员国；肢体；议员；集合元素；构件；家庭成员
definition_en: one of the parts or people that make up a group or a body
core_image: 一张长桌四周坐满人，每把椅子背后贴着写了名字的纸牌
scene: 点名时秘书念出一个名字，长桌尽头有人举手，墙上的名册随即在那一行后面打了一个勾。As the secretary read the roll, a hand went up at the far end of the table, and the list on the wall received a tick beside that member.
sceneCN: 这里 member 指「团体中的一名成员」（第 1 个义项）；句意为点名时长桌尽头有人举手应到，墙上的名册在该成员那一行打勾。可辨识物件：长桌、名册、铅笔、举起的手；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 成员；会员；成员国；肢体；议员；集合元素；构件；家庭成员
成员的；作定语的（如成员国）

derivatives.zh: 会员身份（member + -ship，由「人」转为「身份」）
成员（复数）
非成员（non- + member）
肢解；切去肢体（dis- + member，由「肢体」义派生）

senses.title: One among many
senses.definition: a person who belongs to a group, team or organization
senses.definitionCN: 属于某团体、队伍或组织的一个人
senses.example: Every member of the team signed the card.
senses.exampleCN: 队里的每一名成员都签了卡片。
senses.why: The Latin word for a limb was applied to people as parts of a community, and this is the sense that dominates today.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语指「肢体」的词被用来指共同体中的个人，这成了今天最主要的义项。

senses.title: A state among states
senses.definition: a country or organization that belongs to a larger union
senses.definitionCN: 属于更大联盟的国家或组织
senses.example: The member states met to revise the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 各成员国开会修订这项条约。
senses.why: Once a body can be a part of a larger body, whole states take the name that once belonged to persons.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个机构可以是更大机构的一部分，整个国家也就用上了原属个人的称呼。

senses.title: A limb of the body
senses.definition: an arm, leg or other part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 手臂、腿或身体的其他部位
senses.example: The old anatomy text speaks of the body and its members.
senses.exampleCN: 那本古老的解剖学著作谈到身体及其四肢。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the Latin noun named a limb before it named a person in a group.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：这个拉丁名词先指肢体，后指团体中的人。

senses.title: A seat in the house
senses.definition: a person elected or appointed to a legislative assembly
senses.definitionCN: 经选举或任命进入立法机构的个人
senses.example: The member for the northern district spoke last.
senses.exampleCN: 北部选区的议员最后发言。
senses.why: Legislatures borrow the plain word for a group member and make it a title with a constituency attached.
senses.whyCN: 立法机构借用这个表示团体成员的普通词，并给它加上选区，使之成为头衔。

senses.title: An element of a set
senses.definition: an object that belongs to a mathematical set
senses.definitionCN: 属于某一数学集合的对象
senses.example: Each member of the set shares one property.
senses.exampleCN: 集合中的每个元素都共有一种性质。
senses.why: Mathematics needed a neutral word for what is inside a set, and the everyday noun was precise enough.
senses.whyCN: 数学需要一个中性词来指集合内部的东西，而这个日常名词已经足够精确。

senses.title: A part of a frame
senses.definition: one of the beams or parts that make up a structure
senses.definitionCN: 构成某一结构的梁或其他部件
senses.example: Every member of the truss carries part of the load.
senses.exampleCN: 桁架的每个构件都承担一部分荷载。
senses.why: Engineering returns to the limb sense: a frame is a body, and its beams are its members.
senses.whyCN: 工程学回到了「肢体」义：框架是一个躯体，梁就是它的肢体。

senses.title: One of the household
senses.definition: a person belonging to a family or household
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个家庭或住户的人
senses.example: The household has four members, two of them children.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家庭有四名成员，其中两名是孩子。
senses.why: The smallest group a person belongs to is a household, and the word scales down without changing.
senses.whyCN: 一个人所属的最小团体就是家庭，这个词缩小尺度而含义不变。

senses.title: One of a species group
senses.definition: an organism belonging to a particular group in taxonomy
senses.definitionCN: 在分类学上属于某一类群的生物
senses.example: This species is a member of the rose family.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种是蔷薇科的一员。
senses.why: Natural history treats a family as a body and its species as members, completing the same metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 博物学把一个科当作躯体、把其中的物种当作成员，完成了同一个比喻。

intro.en: Member comes from Latin membrum 'limb, part of the body', which Latin also used for a person as a part of a community. English borrowed it through Old French. Its deeper origin is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: member 来自拉丁 membrum「肢体、身体的一部分」，拉丁语也用这个词指作为共同体之部分的个人。英语经古法语借入。其更深来源尚无定论。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Membrum is well recorded for a limb. The extension to a person who is a part of a group is also Latin, not a later English invention.
items.cn: membrum 指肢体有充分书证。把它扩展到「团体之部分的个人」也发生在拉丁语中，并非英语后来的创造。

items.en: The deeper origin of membrum is generally thought to involve a root for cutting or dividing, but the form is a reconstruction and different handbooks word it differently.
items.cn: membrum 的更深来源一般被认为与表示「切割、划分」的词根有关，但该形式属重构，各家手册的表述也不一致。

items.en: Old French membre carried both the limb sense and the social sense, and English took the word in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 membre 同时带有「肢体」义与社会义，英语在十三世纪借入这个词。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word spread to legislatures, mathematics and engineering, each borrowing the part-of-a-whole image.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个词扩展到立法机构、数学与工程学，每一处都借用了「整体之一部分」的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-Latin form is a reconstruction, so the family image at the base is inferred rather than demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：前拉丁语的形式属重构，因此词底的家庭意象属推断而非实证。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms and one look-alike built on an unrelated root; group two holds words for people who belong to something.
note.cn: 第一组是同根形式，另加一个建在无关词根上的形近词；第二组是表示「属于某处的人」的词。

entries.definition: The status of being a member; member is the person, membership is what that person holds.
entries.definitionCN: 成员的身份；member 是人，membership 是此人所拥有的身份。

entries.definition: To cut a body into parts, built directly on the limb sense of the Latin noun.
entries.definitionCN: 把身体切成数块，直接建在这个拉丁名词的「肢体」义上。

entries.definition: From re- plus memor 'mindful', not from membrum: it means to recall, and only the sound connects it.
entries.definitionCN: 由 re- 加 memor「留心的」构成，并非来自 membrum：意为回想，只有读音把它联系起来。

entries.definition: Also from memor 'mindful'; the shared letters suggest a limb root that is not there.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自 memor「留心的」；相同的字母让人以为有「肢体」词根，其实并没有。

entries.definition: An organization attached to a larger one; a member can be a person or a body, while an affiliate is always an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 附属于更大机构的组织；member 可以是人也可以是机构，而 affiliate 总是机构。

entries.definition: A colleague or linked firm without formal membership; a member holds a defined place on a roll.
entries.definitionCN: 无正式成员身份的同事或关联公司；member 在名册上拥有明确的位置。

entries.definition: A companion or peer, often in a learned society; fellow stresses equality, member stresses inclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 同伴或同侪，常用于学会；fellow 强调平等，member 强调被纳入。

entries.definition: A person who takes part in an event; a participant need not be on any roll, while a member is.
entries.definitionCN: 参与某项活动的人；参与者不必在名册上，而成员则在名册上。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin limb word, the real institutional compounds, and the real derived forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「肢体」词、真实的机构复合词，以及真实的派生形式。

normal.en: A member is a limb of the body of the group: the metaphor is the same at both scales.
normal.cn: 成员是团体的「肢体」：这个比喻在两个尺度上完全一致。

normal.en: The oldest sense is anatomical, which is why dismember means cutting off limbs, not expelling people.
normal.cn: 最古老的义项是解剖学上的，因此 dismember 指切去肢体，而不是开除成员。

normal.en: Compound phrases: member state, family member, staff member, founding member.
normal.cn: 复合搭配：成员国、家庭成员、工作人员、创始成员。

normal.en: A member of parliament is a member first and a representative second, which is why the title keeps the plain word.
normal.cn: 议会议员先是「成员」，其次才是代表，因此这个头衔保留了那个朴素的词。

normal.en: The plural is regular, and the possessive adds an apostrophe with the possessive ending.
normal.cn: 复数按常规变化，所有格则在词尾加撇号与属格标记。

abstract.en: Picture a long table where every chair has a name card taped to its back.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，每把椅子背后都贴着一张写有名字的卡片。

abstract.en: Picture a truss bridge seen as a skeleton, each beam a limb holding the whole up.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桁架桥被看成一具骨架，每根梁都是撑起整体的一肢。

abstract.en: Picture a family photograph in which each face occupies one place in the frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一张全家福，每张脸都在画面里占一个位置。

examples.en: She became a member of the research group in her second year.
examples.cn: 她在第二年成为研究小组的成员。

examples.en: The member states disagreed over the wording of the clause.
examples.cn: 各成员国对条款的措辞意见不一。

examples.en: The fall injured a member of his left hand.
examples.cn: 那次跌倒伤到了他左手的一处肢体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「member = mem（记忆）+ ber」——被记住、被写进名册的人 → 成员、会员

root: 拉丁 membrum「肢体、身体的一部分」；由「躯体之一肢」引申为「团体之一员」。更深词根属重构，不作定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one limb: a person on the roll, a state inside a union, the anatomical limb itself, a seat in a legislature, an element in a set, a beam in a frame, a face in a household, and a species inside a family.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕「一肢」展开：名册上的人、联盟中的国家、解剖意义上的肢体、立法机构中的一席、集合中的元素、框架中的一根梁、家庭中的一张面孔，以及一个科之内的一个物种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long table where every chair carries a name card on its back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌，每把椅子背后都贴着写有名字的卡片。

branches.en: PERSONS AND HOUSEHOLDS: the person on the roll, and the smallest group that person belongs to.
branches.cn: 个人与家庭：名册上的人，以及此人所归属的最小团体。

branches.en: STATES AND UNIONS: a whole country holding a place inside a larger body.
branches.cn: 国家与联盟：整个国家在更大机构中占据一席。

branches.en: THE OLDEST LAYER: the limb itself, the literal body part behind the metaphor.
branches.cn: 最古老的一层：肢体本身，也就是比喻背后那个字面的身体部位。

branches.en: THE SEAT IN THE HOUSE: a legislator whose title keeps the plain word for a group member.
branches.cn: 议会中的一席：立法者的头衔保留了「团体成员」这个朴素说法。

branches.en: PARTS OF STRUCTURED WHOLE: a set element, a structural beam, and a species inside a family.
branches.cn: 结构整体的各个部分：集合元素、结构构件，以及一个科之内的物种。

intro.en: Member is the Latin limb word reshaped in English, and its family runs from anatomy to institutions.
intro.cn: member 是拉丁语「肢体」一词在英语中的变形，其词族从解剖学一直延伸到制度。

latinIntro.en: Latin membrum yields member and dismember; -ship and non- build the social forms. The Latin noun is third-declension in -um, not a verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 membrum 衍生出 member 与 dismember；-ship 与 non- 构成社会义的形式。这个拉丁名词属 -um 第二变格法，并非动词。

items.example: The Latin noun is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是词族的基础。

items.example: Every member of the team signed the card.
items.exampleCN: 队里的每一名成员都签了卡片。

items.example: The members voted on the proposal.
items.exampleCN: 成员们对这项提案进行了表决。

items.example: Membership carries the right to vote.
Nonmembers may visit on weekdays only.
items.exampleCN: 非会员只能在工作日参观。

items.example: The old chronicle describes how they dismembered the statue.
items.exampleCN: 那部旧编年史描述了人们如何把雕像肢解。

items.meaning: the act or result of cutting apart
items.example: The treaty led to the dismemberment of the kingdom.
items.exampleCN: 这项条约导致王国被分裂。

items.example: The member state blocked the proposal.
items.exampleCN: 该成员国否决了这项提案。

definition_zh: 会员身份；全体会员；会员人数；会费；会籍；成员关系；集合的属于关系；会员制
definition_en: the state of belonging to a group, or the members of a group taken together
core_image: 一张塑料会员卡，边缘磨得发白，卡号处有一道被反复摩挲的指印
scene: 旧图书馆的借书台前，管理员把一张磨旧的卡片推回来，说补缴费用后名字才会重新留在名册上。At the old library desk the clerk pushed back a worn card and said her membership would be renewed once the fee was paid.
sceneCN: 这里 membership 指「会员身份」（第 1 个义项：某人作为会员的资格）；句意为管理员把磨旧的卡片推回来，说补缴费用后她的会员身份才会续上。可辨识物件：借书台、磨白的卡片、名册、印章；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 会员身份；全体会员；会员人数；会费；会籍；成员关系；（数学）属于关系；会员制

derivatives.zh: 基础词：成员；会员
非会员；未入会者（non- + member）
复合名词：由会员身份与卡片合成的会员卡，用来证明身份

senses.title: A place on the roll
senses.definition: the state of being a member of a group or organization
senses.definitionCN: 作为某团体或组织的成员而具有的身份
senses.example: Membership gives you a vote at the annual meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会员身份让你在年会上拥有投票权。
senses.why: The suffix -ship names a condition rather than a person: a member is who you are, and membership is the standing that follows.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ship 命名的是状态而非人：成员是你是「谁」，而会员身份是随之而来的地位。

senses.title: Everyone on the roll
senses.definition: the members of an organization considered as one group
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个整体来看的某组织的全体成员
senses.example: The whole membership was invited to the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 全体会员都应邀参加了投票。
senses.why: A collective noun is a short step from the state: if everyone holds the status, the status can name everyone.
senses.whyCN: 从状态到集体名词只差一步：如果人人都拥有这个身份，这个身份就可以用来指所有人。

senses.title: The number counted
senses.definition: the total number of members in a body
senses.definitionCN: 某组织的成员总人数
senses.example: Membership fell below two hundred last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年会员人数降到了两百以下。
senses.why: Once a roll exists it can be counted, and the abstract noun takes on a number.
senses.whyCN: 名册一旦存在就可以清点，这个抽象名词于是带上了数字。

senses.title: The fee on the counter
senses.definition: the amount paid regularly in order to remain a member
senses.definitionCN: 为保留成员身份而定期缴纳的费用
senses.example: The annual membership is due in January.
senses.exampleCN: 年度会费在一月到期缴纳。
senses.why: Institutions turned the status into something sold by the year, and the price borrowed the name of what it bought.
senses.whyCN: 机构把身份变成按年出售的东西，价格便借用了它所购买之物的名字。

senses.title: The term of the card
senses.definition: the period during which a person's status as a member lasts
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的成员身份持续的那段时间
senses.example: She let her membership lapse after the move.
senses.exampleCN: 搬家之后，她的会籍就中断了。
senses.why: A status that can be renewed must also have an end, so the noun covers the span as well as the state.
senses.whyCN: 可以续期的身份也必然有终点，因此这个名词既指状态，也指那段时间。

senses.title: One body inside another
senses.definition: the position of a state or organization as a member of a larger body
senses.definitionCN: 国家或组织作为更大机构成员的地位
senses.example: Membership in the union requires unanimous consent.
senses.exampleCN: 加入该联盟需要全体一致同意。
senses.why: The word leaves persons behind: whole countries can hold membership in a body above them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词越过了个人：整个国家也能在更高一级的机构中拥有成员地位。

senses.title: Belonging to a set
senses.definition: in mathematics, the relation of an element to the set that contains it
senses.definitionCN: 数学中元素与其所属集合之间的关系
senses.example: The proof rests on the membership of every point in the interval.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明依赖于区间内每一点都属于该集合。
senses.why: Logic needed a precise word for one thing being inside another, and borrowed the everyday noun.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学需要一个精确的说法来表示一物处在另一物之中，于是借用了这个日常名词。

senses.title: Sold as a scheme
senses.titleCN: 作为制度出售的会员资格
senses.definition: used before another noun for a paid scheme that grants member benefits
senses.definitionCN: 用在另一名词前，指授予会员权益的付费制度
senses.example: The store pushed its membership programme in every aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 这家商店在每条过道里推销它的会员制度。
senses.why: Commerce compressed the whole relationship into a label, and the label itself became a product.
senses.whyCN: 商业把整段关系压缩成一个标签，而标签本身又成了商品。

intro.en: Membership joins member, from Latin membrum 'limb, part', to the Old English suffix -scipe 'state, condition'. Latin had already extended the limb word to a person who is a part of a body. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: membership 由 member 加古英语后缀 -scipe（表状态、身份）构成；member 来自拉丁 membrum「肢体、部分」。拉丁语已把这个指肢体的词扩展到「作为一个机体之部分的人」。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Membrum meant a limb or a part of the body, and Latin writers extended it to persons as parts of a community. Its deeper origin is generally thought to involve a root for cutting, but that account is a reconstruction rather than a proven form.
items.cn: membrum 意为肢体或身体的一部分，拉丁作者已把它扩展到「共同体之部分的个人」。其更深来源一般被认为与表示「切割」的词根有关，但该说法属重构，并非已证形式。

items.en: -scipe formed nouns of state and condition, as in freondscipe 'friendship'. It is generally thought to be connected with the verb for shaping or creating, and it is the direct source of the modern suffix.
items.cn: -scipe 构成表状态与身份的名词，如 freondscipe「友谊」。它一般被认为与表示「塑造、创造」的动词有关，是现代后缀的直接来源。

items.en: English borrowed membre from Old French in the thirteenth century, and the -b- spelling settled later under Latin influence.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪从古法语借入 membre，拼写中的 -b- 后来在拉丁语影响下固定下来。

items.en: From the sixteenth century member and -ship combined for the state of being a member. The collective sense and the fee sense followed in later commercial use.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，member 与 -ship 组合表示成员身份。集体义与会费义在此后的商业用法中相继出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the root of membrum is a reconstruction, and the first use of the combined noun is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：membrum 的词根属重构，这个组合名词的首见年代也无确切记录。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root words and two near look-alikes whose roots are unrelated; group two holds the words for belonging to an organization.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词，另加两个字形相近却词根无关的词；第二组是表示「归属于某组织」的词。

entries.definition: The person on the roll; membership is the standing that person holds, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 名册上的那个人；membership 是此人所拥有的身份，而不是人本身。

entries.definition: To cut off the limbs of a body, built on the limb sense; it has nothing to do with lists of members.
entries.definitionCN: 切去肢体，建在「肢体」这一义上；它与成员名单毫无关系。

entries.definition: Built on memor 'mindful', not on membrum: it means the act of recalling, despite the similar sound.
entries.definitionCN: 建在 memor「留心的」之上而非 membrum：意为回忆，尽管读音相近。

entries.definition: Shares only the -ship ending; the base is champion, from Latin campus by way of a contest in a field.
entries.definitionCN: 只共用 -ship 后缀；基础词是 champion，经「场地上的竞技」这一路径上溯到拉丁 campus。

entries.definition: A formal connection with a body, often only a listed institution; membership carries rights, dues and a place on the roll.
entries.definitionCN: 与某机构的正式联系，常只是登记一个所属单位；membership 则含权利、会费与名册上的位置。

entries.definition: An organized group of people, or the act of joining; membership is the status inside such a group.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的人群团体，或加入这一团体的行为；membership 是身处其中的身份。

entries.definition: The payment that keeps a service or publication coming; membership may involve a subscription, but it also grants a status.
entries.definitionCN: 维持服务或刊物送达的付款；membership 可能包含订阅费，但它还授予一种身份。

entries.definition: The act of registering on a course or list; membership is the state that follows enrolment.
entries.definitionCN: 在课程或名单上登记的行为；membership 是登记之后持续的状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin limb word, the real suffix of state, and the real phrases used on forms and at counters.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「肢体」词、真实的状态后缀，以及表格与柜台上真实使用的搭配。

normal.en: Member is a limb of a body, and a member is a limb of an organization: the same picture at two scales.
normal.cn: 成员是团体的「肢体」，也是组织的「一肢」：同一幅图在两个尺度上重复。

normal.en: The suffix -ship works the same way in friendship, hardship and membership: it turns a base into a state.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ship 在 friendship、hardship 与 membership 中作用相同：把基础词变成一种状态。

normal.en: Forms say membership card and membership fee, which is where most people meet the word.
normal.cn: 表格上写会员卡与会费，多数人正是从这里认识这个词。

normal.en: A life membership lasts as long as the person; an annual one must be renewed.
normal.cn: 终身会员资格持续到人离世，年度会籍则必须续期。

normal.en: The plural memberships covers several separate memberships held at once.
normal.cn: 复数 memberships 指同时持有的几份会员资格。

abstract.en: Picture a card worn pale at the edges because a thumb has checked it at the door for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一张卡片边缘被磨得发白，因为多年来在门口被拇指反复核对。

abstract.en: Picture a roll on the wall with a tick beside each name, and one line left blank.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的一份名册，每个名字旁有一个勾，只留一行空白。

abstract.en: Picture a country's flag hung inside a larger hall, one flag among many.
abstract.cn: 想象一个国家的旗子挂在一座更大的会堂里，众多旗子中的一面。

examples.en: Membership in the society is open to anyone who applies.
examples.cn: 该学会的会员资格向所有申请者开放。

examples.en: The club raised its membership fee by ten percent.
examples.cn: 这家俱乐部把会费提高了百分之十。

examples.en: Total membership has doubled since the new branch opened.
examples.cn: 自新分部开设以来，会员总数翻了一倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「member（成员）+ ship（船）」——一张船票把你载进名册 → 会员身份、会籍

root: member（拉丁 membrum「肢体、部分」，引申为团体之一员）+ 古英语 -scipe（表状态、身份）；「肢体属于身体」→「人属于团体」。membrum 更深词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one card: the standing it proves, the whole roll behind it, the number on that roll, the fee that keeps the name there, the term before renewal, a body that holds membership in a larger body, an element inside a set, and the paid scheme that sells the whole arrangement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一张卡片展开：卡片所证明的身份、卡片背后的整份名册、名册上的人数、让名字留在名册上的会费、续期之前的期限、一个机构在更大机构中的成员地位、集合中的元素关系，以及把整套安排当作商品出售的会员制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plastic card worn pale at the edges, checked at the door for years.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张边缘磨白的塑料卡片，多年来在门口被反复核对。

branches.en: STATE AND TERM: a place on the roll, and the span of time for which the card stays valid.
branches.cn: 身份与期限：名册上的一个位置，以及卡片保持有效的那段时间。

branches.en: THE ROLL AND ITS COUNT: the members taken together, and the number they add up to.
branches.cn: 名册与清点：合在一起看的全体成员，以及他们累计出的人数。

branches.en: THE PRICE OF THE CARD: the fee that keeps the name on the roll.
branches.cn: 卡片的价格：让名字留在名册上的那笔会费。

branches.en: BODY INSIDE BODY: a state or organization holding membership in a larger union.
branches.cn: 机构之中的机构：国家或组织在更大联盟中的成员地位。

branches.en: LOGIC AND COMMERCE: belonging to a set, and the paid scheme that sells the status.
branches.cn: 逻辑与商业：元素属于集合，以及把身份当作商品出售的会员制。

intro.en: Membership is member plus a suffix of state, and member itself goes back to the Latin word for a limb.
intro.cn: membership 是 member 加一个表状态的后缀，而 member 本身可上溯到拉丁语表示「肢体」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin membrum gives member; Old English -scipe gives the modern -ship, and -s marks the plural. The Latin word has no verb in this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 membrum 给出 member；古英语 -scipe 给出今天的 -ship，-s 标示复数。这个拉丁词在这一词族中没有对应的动词。

items.example: The Latin noun is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是整个词族的基础。

items.structure: membrum + -er (English form of the Latin noun)
items.example: Each member of the team signed the card.
items.exampleCN: 队里的每一名成员都签了卡片。

items.example: The members voted on the proposal.
items.exampleCN: 成员们对这项提案进行了表决。

items.example: Membership gives you a vote at the annual meeting.
items.exampleCN: 会员身份让你在年会上拥有投票权。

items.example: He holds memberships in two learned societies.
items.exampleCN: 他在两个学会都拥有会员资格。

items.example: Nonmembers pay a higher entrance fee.
items.exampleCN: 非会员需付更高的入场费。

items.meaning: to cut off the limbs of a body
items.example: The old penalty was to dismember the body.
items.exampleCN: 古代的刑罚是把身体肢解。

items.meaning: the act or result of cutting apart
items.example: The chronicle records the dismemberment of the kingdom.
items.exampleCN: 编年史记下了王国的分裂。

definition_zh: 纪念碑；纪念馆；纪念的；追悼会；陈述书
definition_en: a statue, building or ceremony that keeps a person or event in public memory; also an adjective meaning held in remembrance
core_image: 一块立在草地上的石碑，碑面朝着一排常来放花的人
scene: 清明前后，山坡上那块石碑前又摆了几束野花，碑上的名字被雨水冲得发亮。A small memorial stands at the bend of the road where the bridge once crossed the stream.
sceneCN: 这里 memorial 是「纪念碑」（第 1 个义项：为使人不忘记而立的石碑）；句意为道路拐弯处立着一座小小的纪念碑，那里曾经有桥跨过溪水。

pos.zh: 纪念碑；纪念馆；追悼会；陈述书
纪念的；悼念的

由 memorialize 再加 -ation 构成，义为「纪念的行为」
由 memorial 加 -ly 构成，义为「以纪念的方式」

senses.title: A structure that keeps a person or event in mind
senses.definition: a statue, building or stone put up so that people do not forget a person or an event
senses.definitionCN: 为使人不忘记某人或某事而立起的雕像、建筑或石碑
senses.example: A stone memorial stands where the school once was.
senses.exampleCN: 学校旧址上立着一座石碑。
senses.why: Latin memor means mindful, so a memorial is first of all an object placed on the ground to hold a memory in one spot for everyone who passes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 memor 意为「记得的」，所以 memorial 首先是一件落在地上的物件，把记忆固定在一处，交给每个经过的人。

senses.title: Existing to honour the dead
senses.definition: used of an object, day or event that exists in order to honour someone who has died
senses.definitionCN: 形容某件物品、某个日子或某场活动是为悼念逝者而设
senses.example: The memorial garden was planted with white roses along its low wall.
senses.exampleCN: 那座纪念园沿着矮墙种满了白玫瑰。
senses.why: Once the purpose of the stone is folded into an adjective, the word stops pointing at the object and starts describing the mood of everything arranged around it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦石头的用途被折叠进形容词，这个词就不再指向物件本身，而开始形容围绕它安排的一切所带的气氛。

senses.title: A ceremony held so that people remember together
senses.definition: a service or gathering at which people recall someone or something as a group
senses.definitionCN: 让人们聚在一起共同追忆某人或某事的仪式或聚会
senses.example: The memorial lasted an hour, and nobody spoke of anything else.
senses.exampleCN: 追悼会开了一个小时，没有人谈别的事。
senses.why: Memory in Latin is a private act, but when a group gathers to keep it, the word stretches from the stone to the hour spent standing beside it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语里的记忆是私人的行为，可一旦一群人聚起来共同守着它，词就从那块石头延伸到站在石头旁度过的那一个小时。

senses.title: A written statement laid before a government
senses.definition: a formal document that sets out facts or a request and is handed to someone in authority
senses.definitionCN: 把事实或请求写明、递交给掌权者的正式文书
senses.example: The merchants sent a memorial to the council asking for lower tolls.
senses.exampleCN: 商人们向议会递交了一份陈述书，请求降低通行费。
senses.why: A written record is memory made public, so this word once named a paper that kept an argument standing in front of those who held power.
senses.whyCN: 书面记录是把记忆公开，所以这个词曾经指一份文书，让理由一直立在掌权者眼前。

intro.en: Memorial descends from the Latin word for mindful, and it travelled through the language of memory into English as both a stone and an adjective of remembrance.
intro.cn: memorial 源自拉丁语中表示「记得」的词，经过一整套关于记忆的词汇进入英语，既指一块石头，也作表示悼念的形容词。

items.en: Memor was the Latin adjective for mindful or remembering, and it was used of a person who kept something in mind.
items.cn: memor 是拉丁语里表示「记得的、留心的」形容词，用来形容把某事放在心上的人。

items.en: Memoria named memory itself, both the faculty and the thing remembered, and it fed a large family of words.
items.cn: memoria 指记忆本身，既是记忆力，也是被记住的事，并派生出一大批词。

items.en: Memorialis was formed on memoria with a suffix meaning relating to, so it meant belonging to memory.
items.cn: memorialis 由 memoria 加表示「与……有关」的后缀构成，意为属于记忆的。

items.en: Old French passed the word to English, where it first named a record or a written statement as much as a stone.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词传给英语，早期它既指石碑，也同样指记录或书面陈述。

items.en: Modern English keeps the stone, the ceremony and the adjective, while the written-statement sense survives mainly in historical and official use.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了石碑、仪式与形容词三个用法，而「书面陈述」一义主要留在历史与公文语境里。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin word for memory through its English family; the near-meaning group gathers the objects and words used to honour what has been lost.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中表示「记忆」的词串起它的英语词族；近义组收用来向逝去之物致敬的物件与说法。

entries.definition: The ability to keep things in mind, and something kept that way.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物留在心里的能力，以及被这样留住的东西。

entries.definition: To learn something by heart until it can be repeated.
entries.definitionCN: 把内容记到能复述为止。

entries.definition: Worth being remembered because it is unusual or moving.
entries.definitionCN: 因不寻常或动人而值得被记住的。

entries.definition: A short note written so that a point is not forgotten.
entries.definitionCN: 为防止要点被忘掉而写下的简短记录。

entries.definition: A building or statue built to keep a person or event famous.
entries.definitionCN: 为让某人或某事长留人心而建的建筑或雕像。

entries.definition: The act of keeping someone in mind, often in a ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人留在心里的行为，常出现在仪式中。

entries.definition: Something said or done to show respect and admiration.
entries.definitionCN: 为表达敬意与钦佩而说的话或做的事。

entries.definition: Made or held in order to honour a person or event.
entries.definitionCN: 为纪念某人或某事而制作或举行的。

normalIntro.en: One Latin root for remembering runs through this whole family, and the word leans on it whether it names a stone, a service or a piece of paper.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「记得」的拉丁词根贯穿整族词，无论是石碑、仪式还是一纸文书，这个词都靠它立住。

normal.en: Memor is Latin for mindful, so a memorial is an object whose only job is to keep something in mind.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 memor 意为记得，所以 memorial 是一件唯一职责就是让人记住某事的物件。

normal.en: Memory, memorize and memorable all sit on the same root, which is why they look and sound so close.
normal.cn: memory、memorize 与 memorable 都长在同一个词根上，所以它们的样子与读音都这么近。

normal.en: The adjective memorial keeps the noun's purpose but drops the object, so a memorial service honours without any stone present.
normal.cn: 形容词 memorial 保留名词的用途却丢掉物件，所以 memorial service 可以在没有石头的情况下完成悼念。

normal.en: Old use of memorial for a petition survives in the phrase memorial to the council, where paper replaces stone.
normal.cn: memorial 指请愿书的旧用法还活在向议会递交文书的说法里，纸取代了石头。

normal.en: Memorial Day is capitalized because it names a fixed public holiday, not any stone you happen to pass.
normal.cn: Memorial Day 首字母大写，因为它指一个固定的公共节日，而不是你路过的一块石头。

abstract.en: Stone is the slowest thing a town owns, so putting a name on it is a way of asking it to outlast every voice that could say the name.
abstract.cn: 石头是一座城镇拥有的最慢的东西，把名字刻上去，就是请它比所有能念出这个名字的嗓子活得更久。

abstract.en: A ceremony and a slab do the same work: both hold a memory still so that a crowd can look at it together.
abstract.cn: 仪式与石板做同一件事：都把一段记忆按住，好让一群人能一起看着它。

abstract.en: The word began as an adjective of the mind and ended up on stone, which says that remembering always wants something solid to lean on.
abstract.cn: 这个词起于一个关于心智的形容词，最后落到石头上，说明记忆总想找点坚实的东西靠着。

examples.en: A memorial was built beside the river for the men lost at sea.
examples.cn: 河边立起一座纪念碑，纪念那些在海上失踪的人。

examples.en: The memorial service ended with a single bell.
examples.cn: 追悼仪式在一声钟响中结束。

examples.en: Each spring the town holds a small memorial in the old square.
examples.cn: 每年春天，镇上都在旧广场举行一场小小的纪念活动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫忘」——碑立在那里，就是叫人莫忘；记住 memorial 是纪念碑。

root: 拉丁语 memor（记得的）+ -ia（名词词尾）→ memoria（记忆）→ 晚期拉丁语 memorialis（属于记忆的）→ 古法语 memorial → 英语 memorial。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an object or act that keeps memory fixed. It splits into the stone, the adjective of honour, the shared ceremony, and the paper that puts a case before power.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把记忆固定住的物件或行为。它分出石碑、表示敬意的形容词、众人共办的仪式，以及把理由递到权力面前的文书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone standing in grass, with fresh flowers at its foot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块立在草里的石碑，脚边放着新花。

branches.en: a stone slab under bare trees
branches.cn: 光秃的树下的一块石板

branches.en: white roses along a low wall
branches.cn: 矮墙边的一排白玫瑰

branches.en: people standing in a cold hall
branches.cn: 人们站在冷清的礼堂里

branches.en: a folded paper handed to a clerk
branches.cn: 一份折好的文书递给书记员

branches.en: a name cut into stone so that it outlasts a voice
branches.cn: 刻进石头的名字，比声音活得更久

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun of memory fitted with a suffix of relation, and English later added endings that turn it into a verb and an adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示记忆的名词加上一个表关系的后缀，英语后来又添上词尾，把它变成动词与副词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 记忆；记住并回想信息的能力，也可指一段回忆、纪念或计算机存储
definition_en: the ability to remember information and experiences, a remembered event, or the part of a computer that stores data
core_image: 一间库房按编号存放过往片段，取件时按编号调出
scene: 老人闻到医院走廊的消毒水味，立刻想起多年前陪护家人的那个下午。The smell of disinfectant in the corridor brings back the afternoon years ago when she sat beside a sick relative, a sudden act of memory.
sceneCN: 这里 memory 指「唤起过往经历的能力」（第 1 个义项：把过去的片段重新调出）；句意为消毒水的气味让她立刻回到多年前陪护家人的那个下午。图中可辨识物件：医院走廊、消毒水瓶、长椅、被唤起的时间线；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: The ability to remember
senses.definition: the faculty by which information and past experiences are stored and recalled
senses.definitionCN: 储存并调取信息与过往经历的能力
senses.example: The smell of disinfectant brings back that afternoon at once.
senses.exampleCN: 消毒水的气味立刻把她带回那个下午。
senses.why: memory names a capacity before it names any particular content: the cupboard exists before the things put in it.
senses.whyCN: memory 先命名一种能力，再命名具体内容：柜子先存在，东西才放进去。

senses.title: A remembered event
senses.definition: a particular past event that one can recall
senses.definitionCN: 能够回想起来的一件具体往事
senses.example: Her earliest memory is of a blue door.
senses.exampleCN: 她最早的记忆是一扇蓝色的门。
senses.why: the mass noun becomes countable when a single episode is pulled out of the store and held up.
senses.whyCN: 当单个片段被从库房里取出并举起时，不可数名词就变成可数。

senses.title: The content stored
senses.definition: the information or impression retained about something
senses.definitionCN: 关于某事物所保留的信息或印象
senses.example: His memory of the route was better than the map.
senses.exampleCN: 他对路线的记忆比地图还准。
senses.why: what is stored is not the event but a trace of it, which is why memory can be accurate and wrong at the same time.
senses.whyCN: 被储存的不是事件本身，而是事件的痕迹；因此记忆可以既准确又出错。

senses.title: Remembrance and commemoration
senses.definition: the keeping of someone or something in respectful remembrance
senses.definitionCN: 以敬意把某人或某事留在怀念中
senses.example: A bench was placed in memory of the teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 一张长椅被安放以纪念这位老师。
senses.why: the word widens from an individual's store to a community's shared keeping, and the phrase in memory of marks that shift.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从个人的储存扩展到群体的共同保存；「为纪念……」这一短语标记了这种转移。

senses.title: Reputation after death
senses.definition: the way a person is remembered by later generations
senses.definitionCN: 后人对某人的记忆与评价
senses.example: The engineer left a memory of honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 这位工程师留下了诚实的名声。
senses.why: if memory is what survives, then a person's memory is the part of them that outlives them.
senses.whyCN: 如果 memory 是留存下来的东西，那么一个人的 memory 就是比他活得更久的那部分。

senses.title: Computer memory
senses.definition: the electronic storage in a computer that holds data and programs for immediate use
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中存放数据与程序以供即时使用的电子存储
senses.example: The program needs more memory than the laptop has.
senses.exampleCN: 这个程序需要的内存超过这台笔记本的容量。
senses.why: the machine metaphor is literal: data is put in, kept, and taken out, exactly like a remembered thing.
senses.whyCN: 机器的比喻是字面的：数据被放入、保存、取出，和记住的东西完全一样。

senses.title: Storage capacity
senses.definition: the amount of data a device or medium can hold
senses.definitionCN: 设备或介质能够容纳的数据量
senses.example: The phone has sixty-four gigabytes of memory.
senses.exampleCN: 这部手机有六十四吉字节的存储。
senses.why: once storage is a place, it can be measured like shelf space, so the noun shifts from the place to its size.
senses.whyCN: 存储一旦成为场所，就能像货架空间那样被计量，于是名词从场所转为容量。

senses.title: A memorial object or rite
senses.definition: an object, day or ceremony that keeps someone or something in mind
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某事留在心上的物品、日子或仪式
senses.example: The village holds a memory ceremony every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄每年春天举行纪念仪式。
senses.why: a memorial is memory externalized, made visible so that forgetting becomes harder.
senses.whyCN: 纪念物是记忆的外化，被做成看得见的东西，使遗忘更困难。

senses.title: A type of memory system
senses.definition: a named subsystem such as working, short-term or long-term memory
senses.definitionCN: 被命名的子系统，如工作记忆、短时记忆或长时记忆
senses.example: Working memory holds a phone number just long enough to dial.
senses.exampleCN: 工作记忆把电话号码保留到拨完为止。
senses.why: research splits the cupboard into compartments, and each compartment inherits the same word.
senses.whyCN: 研究把柜子分成隔间，每个隔间都继承同一个词。

intro.en: Memory comes from Latin memoria, from memor 'mindful', and reached English through Old French. The computing sense is twentieth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: memory 来自拉丁 memoria，源自 memor「记得的」，经古法语进入英语。计算义是 20 世纪的延伸。年代为约数。

items.en: Memor was an adjective meaning 'mindful, remembering'; it described a person who keeps something in mind.
items.cn: memor 是形容词，意为「记得的、留心的」，描述把某事放在心上的人。

items.en: Memoria 'memory, remembrance, the faculty of remembering' was built on memor and named both the capacity and its content.
items.cn: memoria「记忆、怀念、记忆力」由 memor 构成，同时命名能力与内容。

items.en: Old French memorie carried the word into English in the thirteenth century; the ending settled as -y.
items.cn: 古法语 memorie 在 13 世纪把词带入英语；词尾最终固定为 -y。

items.en: The deeper root is reconstructed as *men- 'to think', also present in mind and in Greek mnēmē 'memory'.
items.cn: 更早的词根被重构为 *men-「思考」，也出现在英语的「心智」一词与希腊语 mnēmē「记忆」中。

items.en: Memory in the machine sense dates from the 1940s, when early computers stored instructions electronically.
items.cn: 机器义的 memory 形成于 20 世纪 40 年代，当时早期计算机以电子方式存储指令。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the exact first English use of the computing sense is not fixed, and the pre-Latin history of memor is reconstructed rather than directly attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：计算义的最早英语用法没有确切年代；memor 在拉丁语之前的历史属于重构，而非直接书证。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same memor family that are easily swapped; group two holds words about bringing the past back.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 memor 词族里容易混用的词；第二组是关于把过去重新带回的词。

entries.definition: To commit something to memory deliberately; memory is the store, memorize is the act of putting something in.
entries.definitionCN: 有意把某物记入记忆；memory 是库房，memorize 是放入的动作。

entries.definition: Something built or held to remember a person or event; it externalizes memory rather than naming the faculty.
entries.definitionCN: 为纪念某人或某事而建或举行的东西；把记忆外化，而非命名能力。

entries.definition: Worthy of being remembered; it judges the content, while memory names the container.
entries.definitionCN: 值得记住的；评判内容，而 memory 命名容器。

entries.definition: A note made so that something will not be forgotten; Latin memorare 'to mention' supplies it, not the noun memory directly.
entries.definitionCN: 为防止遗忘而写的备忘；来自拉丁 memorare「提及」，并非直接由名词 memory 派生。

entries.definition: The act of bringing something back to mind; memory is the store, recall is the hand that reaches in.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物重新带回心头的动作；memory 是库房，recall 是伸进去的手。

entries.definition: The process of piecing a past scene together; it often implies effort and partial reconstruction.
entries.definitionCN: 把过去场景一块块拼回来的过程；常暗示费力与部分重建。

entries.definition: The act of keeping someone in mind, often with ceremony; it leans toward commemoration rather than storage.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人留在心上的行为，常伴仪式；偏向纪念而非储存。

entries.definition: The degree to which learned material remains available over time; it measures memory's durability.
entries.definitionCN: 所学材料随时间保留的程度；衡量记忆的持久性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: memor 'mindful' + -y gives memory; the same stem runs through memorize, memorial and memorable.
normal.cn: memor「记得的」+ -y 构成 memory；同一词干贯穿 memorize、memorial 与 memorable。

normal.en: The family runs memorize, memorization, memorial, memorable and remembrance.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 memorize、memorization、memorial、memorable 与 remembrance。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: from memory, in memory of, working memory, memory loss.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：凭记忆、为纪念、工作记忆、记忆丧失。

normal.en: In computing, memory is a place; in psychology, it is both a place and a capacity.
normal.cn: 在计算机领域，memory 是场所；在心理学中，它既是场所也是能力。

normal.en: Memory is the cupboard, recall is the act of opening it.
normal.cn: memory 是柜子，recall 是打开柜子的动作。

abstract.en: Picture a dark warehouse where every box is labelled by date.
abstract.cn: 想象一座昏暗的库房，每个箱子都按日期贴标签。

abstract.en: Picture a smell that opens a door you did not know was there.
abstract.cn: 想象一种气味打开了一扇你不知道存在的门。

abstract.en: Picture a stone bench that keeps saying one name without sound.
abstract.cn: 想象一张石凳无声地反复说着一个名字。

examples.en: He recited the poem from memory.
examples.cn: 他凭记忆背诵了这首诗。

examples.en: The garden was planted in memory of her mother.
examples.cn: 这座花园是为纪念她母亲而种的。

examples.en: The update needs more memory than the old tablet has.
examples.cn: 这次更新需要的内存超过旧平板电脑的容量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没魔力」——记得住不是因为魔力，而是因为反复回看 → 记忆

root: 拉丁 memoria「记忆」← memor「记得的」；更早可重构为印欧语 *men-「思考」，与 mind、希腊语 mnēmē 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one cupboard: the capacity, one recalled event, the stored content, communal keeping, posthumous reputation, the machine's store, its size, the visible memorial and the named subsystem.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一间库房展开：能力、一段回忆、所存内容、共同保存、身后名声、机器存储、容量、可见的纪念物，以及被命名的子系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a numbered store from which a past piece is fetched on demand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座编号库房，按需把过去的片段取出。

branches.en: THE STORE AND ITS PIECES: capacity, one event, and the trace that remains.
branches.cn: 库房与片段：能力、单件往事，以及留下的痕迹。

branches.en: OUTWARD KEEPING: memory leaves the head as a ceremony or a bench.
branches.cn: 向外的保存：记忆以仪式或长椅的形式离开脑袋。

branches.en: AFTER LIFE: what survives of a person is precisely their memory in others.
branches.cn: 身后：一个人留下来的，正是他在别人心中的记忆。

branches.en: MACHINE: the same cupboard is built in silicon and then measured in gigabytes.
branches.cn: 机器：同一间库房用硅造出来，再以吉字节计量。

branches.en: COMPARTMENTS: research divides the cupboard and names each shelf.
branches.cn: 隔间：研究把柜子分开，并给每层架子命名。

intro.en: Memory is a Latin adjective turned noun: memor plus -y. The same stem builds a large family of verbs, adjectives and monuments.
intro.cn: memory 是拉丁形容词变来的名词：memor 加 -y。同一词干构成一大批动词、形容词与纪念物。

latinIntro.en: Latin memor 'mindful' gives memoria and memorare; English draws memory, memorize, memorial, memorable and remembrance from this line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 memor「记得的」生成 memoria 与 memorare；英语由此得到 memory、memorize、memorial、memorable 与 remembrance。

items.example: Memor is the adjective behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: memor 是整个词族背后的形容词。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成名词。

items.example: Memoria named both the power and its content.
items.exampleCN: memoria 同时命名能力与内容。

items.meaning: the faculty or content of remembering
items.example: Memory can be trained but not enlarged at will.
items.exampleCN: 记忆可以训练，却不能随意扩容。

items.meaning: the act of committing to memory
a thing that keeps a person in mind
items.exampleCN: 纪念碑上列出了每个名字。

items.meaning: to honour by keeping in memory
items.exampleCN: 这块铭牌纪念那次救援。
