senses.title: Of the mind
senses.titleCN: 心智的：发生在头脑里的事
senses.definition: relating to the mind or to thinking, as opposed to the body
senses.definitionCN: 与心智或思维有关的，与身体相对
senses.example: Reading a map is a mental skill, not a physical one.
senses.exampleCN: 看地图是一项心智技能，而不是体力技能。
senses.why: Mental entered English in the early 15th century from Late Latin mentalis, from Latin mens 'mind'. The adjective simply marks what happens inside the head.
senses.whyCN: mental 于 15 世纪初从晚期拉丁语 mentalis 进入英语，源自拉丁语 mens“心智”。这个形容词只标记在头脑内部发生的事。

senses.title: Psychological health
senses.titleCN: 心理的：情绪与心理状态
senses.definition: relating to a person's emotional and psychological condition
senses.definitionCN: 与一个人的情绪与心理状况有关的
senses.example: The clinic offers mental health services for teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为青少年提供心理健康服务。
senses.why: Mental health is recorded from 1803. Once the mind has a health of its own, the adjective moves from describing thought to naming a field of care.
senses.whyCN: mental health 自 1803 年有记录。一旦心智有了自己的健康，这个形容词就从描述思维转为命名一个照护领域。

senses.title: Of the soul
senses.titleCN: 精神的：心灵层面的旧义
senses.definition: in older use, relating to the soul or the inner, spiritual life
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，与灵魂或内在精神生活有关的
senses.example: The old prayer asks for mental peace rather than bodily comfort.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古老的祷文求的是心灵的安宁，而不是身体的舒适。
senses.why: In Middle English, mental also meant 'of the soul, spiritual'. Before medicine divided mind from body, the word covered the whole inner life.
senses.whyCN: 在中古英语里，mental 也意为“灵魂的、精神的”。在医学把心智与身体分开之前，这个词覆盖的是整个内在生活。

senses.title: Intellectual effort
senses.titleCN: 脑力的：劳动落在头脑上
senses.definition: requiring or involving thought and intellect rather than physical work
senses.definitionCN: 需要或涉及思考与智力，而非体力劳动
senses.example: Mental labour can exhaust a person as surely as lifting does.
senses.exampleCN: 脑力劳动照样能把人累垮，就像搬运一样。
senses.why: From the 1520s the word meant 'done or performed in the mind'. Effort shifts from the muscles to the brain, and the adjective follows it.
senses.whyCN: 自 16 世纪 20 年代起，这个词意为“在头脑中完成的”。力气从肌肉转到大脑，形容词也跟着转了过去。

senses.title: Done inside the head
senses.titleCN: 默算默想：不外化的过程
senses.definition: performed silently in the mind, without writing or speaking
senses.definitionCN: 不写出来也不说出来，在脑中默默完成
senses.example: She did the sum mentally and wrote only the answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她心算了那道题，只写下答案。
senses.why: Mental arithmetic keeps the whole operation invisible. The adjective marks work that leaves no trace until the result appears.
senses.whyCN: 心算把整个运算过程藏了起来。这个形容词标记的是那种直到结果出现才留下痕迹的劳动。

senses.title: Psychiatric illness
senses.definition: relating to psychiatric illness, its institutions and its patients
senses.definitionCN: 与精神疾病、其机构及病人有关的
senses.example: He was admitted to a mental hospital after the second episode.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次发作后，他被送进了精神病院。
senses.why: Mental patient is recorded from 1859 and mental hospital from 1891. Once institutions exist, the adjective becomes a clinical address.
senses.whyCN: mental patient 自 1859 年有记录，mental hospital 自 1891 年有记录。一旦机构存在，这个形容词就变成了一个临床门牌号。

senses.title: Slang: crazy
senses.titleCN: 口语：发疯的、脑子有毛病的
senses.definition: in informal British English, crazy or wildly unreasonable
senses.definitionCN: 在英式口语中，指发疯的或极不合理的
senses.example: You are mental if you think that jump is safe.
senses.exampleCN: 你要是觉得那样跳下去没事，那你真是疯了。
senses.why: The slang sense 'crazy, deranged' is recorded from 1927, probably from combinations such as mental patient. A clinical label leaks into the playground.
senses.whyCN: “发疯的、精神错乱的”这一俚语义自 1927 年有记录，很可能来自 mental patient 一类的组合。临床标签漏进了操场。

senses.title: Slang noun: a mad person
senses.definition: in informal British English, a person who is mentally ill or behaves wildly
senses.definitionCN: 在英式口语中，指精神失常或行为失控的人
senses.example: The driver was a complete mental and should never have been on the road.
senses.exampleCN: 那个司机完全是个疯子，根本就不该上路。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective into a noun for a person who has the quality. Here the medical label becomes an insult.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把形容词直接变成指人的名词。在这里，医学标签变成了骂人的话。

senses.title: Legal and clinical capacity
senses.definition: in law and medicine, used of a person's ability to understand, decide and be responsible
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与医学中，指一个人理解、决定与承担责任的能力
senses.example: The court asked whether the accused had the mental capacity to understand the charge.
senses.exampleCN: 法院问的是被告是否有心智能力理解这项指控。
senses.why: Law needs the mind as a measurable fact, not a metaphor. Mental capacity turns the inner life into something a form can record.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要把心智当成可测量的事实，而不是比喻。mental capacity 把内在生活变成表格上可以填写的东西。

intro.en: Mental comes from Latin mens (genitive mentis) 'mind' through Late Latin mentalis. Its root is PIE *men- 'to think'. The medical and middle senses of the letters 'ment' belong to other roots entirely. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mental 经由晚期拉丁语 mentalis 来自拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）“心智”。它的词根是原始印欧语 *men-“思考”。字母 ment 所对应的“医疗”与“中间”两族词，属于完全另外的词根。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded as 'in, of, or pertaining to the mind; characteristic of the intellect'. It came from Late Latin mentalis 'of the mind', an adjective built on Latin mens.
items.cn: 最早记录为“在心智之中的、属于心智的；智力特征的”。它来自晚期拉丁语 mentalis“心智的”，是建立在拉丁语 mens 之上的形容词。

items.en: Latin mens (genitive mentis) means 'mind, intellect, thought, intention'. The stem ment- is what English borrows in mental, mentality and dementia.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）意为“心智、智力、思想、意图”。英语在 mental、mentality、dementia 中借入的正是词干 ment-。

items.en: The root *men- (1) means 'to think'. It also lies behind English mind, a native Germanic cousin of Latin mens rather than a borrowing from it.
items.cn: 词根 *men-（第一支）意为“思考”。它也是英语 mind 的来源——mind 是拉丁语 mens 在日耳曼语里的本族表亲，而不是从拉丁语借来的。

items.en: Mental also meant 'of the soul, spiritual' in Middle English. The word covered the inner life before medicine separated mind from body.
items.cn: 在中古英语里，mental 也意为“灵魂的、精神的”。在医学把心智与身体分开之前，这个词覆盖的是整个内在生活。

items.en: The sense 'done or performed in the mind' is recorded, the sense behind mental arithmetic and mental rehearsal.
items.cn: 记录到“在头脑中完成的”这一义项，它正是 mental arithmetic 与 mental rehearsal 背后的意思。

items.en: Mental health is recorded from 1803, mental illness from 1819, mental patient from 1859 and mental hospital from 1891. The slang sense 'crazy, deranged' follows in 1927, probably from those combinations.
items.cn: mental health 自 1803 年有记录，mental illness 自 1819 年，mental patient 自 1859 年，mental hospital 自 1891 年。俚语义“发疯的、精神错乱的”在 1927 年出现，很可能来自这些组合。

note.en: The first group separates the native noun mind, the derived noun mentality, the adverb and the person word. The second group places mental against the adjectives it is most often confused with, including its usual opposite.
note.cn: 第一组区分本族名词 mind、派生名词 mentality、副词与指人的词。第二组把 mental 与最常混淆的几个形容词放在一起，包括它通常的对立面。

entries.definition: the faculty of thinking, or a person's thoughts and attention. It is the native English cousin of Latin mens, while mental is the borrowed adjective built on mens.
entries.definitionCN: 思维的能力，或一个人的想法与注意力。它是拉丁语 mens 在英语里的本族表亲，而 mental 是建立在 mens 上的借入形容词。

entries.definition: a typical way of thinking, or the level of a person's intellectual power. It is a countable pattern of mind, not a synonym of mental.
entries.definitionCN: 典型的思维方式，或一个人的智力水平。它是可数的思维模式，不是 mental 的同义词。

entries.definition: in the mind, or with respect to the mind. It modifies a verb ('mentally rehearsed') where mental would modify a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在脑中，或就心智而言。它修饰动词（如 mentally rehearsed），而 mental 修饰名词。

entries.definition: a performer who appears to read minds, or a believer in mentalism. It never means 'a mental person'.
entries.definitionCN: 看似能读心的表演者，或心灵主义的信奉者。它从不表示“精神失常的人”。

entries.definition: relating to the study of the mind and behaviour, or to a person's inner emotional state. It is more technical than mental and often replaces it in careful writing.
entries.definitionCN: 与心理学研究或一个人的内在情绪状态有关的。它比 mental 更技术化，在严谨写作中常替代 mental。

entries.definition: relating to the medical treatment of mental illness. It names the clinic, while mental can still be a neutral word for the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 与精神疾病的医学治疗有关的。它命名的是临床，而 mental 仍可中性地指心智。

entries.definition: relating to the intellect and its exercise, especially in learning and analysis. It praises the work of the mind; mental merely locates it.
entries.definitionCN: 与智力及其运用有关的，尤其在学习与分析中。它赞赏头脑的工作；mental 只标明位置。

entries.definition: relating to the body rather than the mind. The pair mental and physical organises everyday talk about health, training and fatigue.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体而非心智有关的。mental 与 physical 这一对词组织起了日常关于健康、训练与疲劳的说法。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin mens (genitive mentis) 'mind', PIE *men- 'to think', the English cousin mind, and the family mentality, mentally, dementia.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）“心智”、原始印欧语 *men-“思考”、英语表亲 mind，以及 mentality、mentally、dementia 词族。

normal.en: mens, mentis means 'mind'. Mental is the adjective of that noun: whatever belongs to the mind.
normal.cn: mens、mentis 意为“心智”。mental 就是这个名词的形容词：一切属于心智的东西。

normal.en: The root *men- means 'to think', and it also gives the native English word mind. Mental is the borrowed twin of mind.
normal.cn: 词根 *men- 意为“思考”，它也给出英语本族词 mind。mental 是 mind 的借入版双胞胎。

normal.en: mentality is mental plus -ity: not the mind itself but its habitual shape, a way of thinking.
normal.cn: mentality 是 mental 加 -ity：不是心智本身，而是它习惯性的形状，即一种思维方式。

normal.en: mentally is the adverb: it tells you where the work happens, as in mentally rehearsed.
normal.cn: mentally 是副词：它告诉你工作发生在哪里，如 mentally rehearsed（在脑中排练）。

normal.en: Keep the fixed phrases straight: mental health, mental illness, mental hospital. These are clinical and neutral, not insults.
normal.cn: 把固定搭配记准：mental health、mental illness、mental hospital。这些是临床且中性的说法，不是骂人。

abstract.en: Picture a lit lamp inside a skull. Nobody outside can see the flame, only its light falling on what the person does next.
abstract.cn: 想象颅骨里点着一盏灯。外面的人看不见火焰，只看见火光落在这个人接下来的动作上。

abstract.en: The same lamp can be described in three registers: mental is everyday, psychological is scientific, psychiatric is clinical. One flame, three vocabularies.
abstract.cn: 同一盏灯可以用三种语域描述：mental 是日常的，psychological 是科学的，psychiatric 是临床的。一团火焰，三套词汇。

abstract.en: Because the light is invisible, the word is easily abused: it can name care, or it can become an insult. The phrase tells you which.
abstract.cn: 正因为光看不见，这个词容易被滥用：它可以命名照护，也可以变成侮辱。是哪个，要看它所在的短语。

examples.en: The injury healed in weeks, but the mental scars took years.
examples.cn: 伤在几周内就愈合了，但心理上的伤痕花了好几年。

examples.en: He ran the whole interview in his head, mentally correcting every answer.
examples.cn: 他在脑子里把整场面试过了一遍，逐条修正每个回答。

examples.en: The report calls for better mental health care in rural schools.
examples.cn: 报告呼吁改善乡村学校的心理健康照护。

dict_mnemonic.text: “门头儿”——门头儿里面亮着一盏灯，那是脑子里转个不停的念头 → mental 心理的、心智的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）“心智”，词根 *men- 意为“思考”，核心是“在头脑内部进行的活动”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of mental, all lit by one lamp inside the skull: first it simply marks where thought happens, then it names health, effort, silence, illness, insult and finally a legal fact.
sensesIntro.cn: mental 的九个义项都被颅骨里的同一盏灯照亮：它先只标记思考发生的位置，继而命名健康、劳动、沉默、疾病、辱骂，最后成为一种法律事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp burning inside a skull, visible only through what the person does.
core.cn: 核心意象：颅骨里燃着的一盏灯，只能通过这个人的举动被看见。

branches.en: THE INNER LIFE: the oldest sense marks the mind, and once also the soul, as a region distinct from the body.
branches.cn: 内在生活：最老的义项标记心智——也曾标记灵魂——作为区别于身体的一个区域。

branches.en: HEALTH: mental health gives the inner life a condition that can be cared for.
branches.cn: 健康：mental health 给内在生活一个可以被照护的状态。

branches.en: EFFORT: thought becomes labour, and labour can be done with no visible trace.
branches.cn: 劳动：思考变成劳作，而这种劳作可以不留可见痕迹。

branches.en: ILLNESS: the clinical label builds hospitals and patients, and then turns into a playground insult.
branches.cn: 疾病：临床标签建起了医院与病人，随后又变成操场上的骂人话。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT: slang decides who is crazy; law decides who can understand and be responsible.
branches.cn: 判断：俚语义断定谁疯了；法律则断定谁能理解、谁能负责。

intro.en: Mental is Latin ment- 'mind' plus the adjective ending -al. The suffix is productive in English; the stem ment- is not a free word, but it recurs in mentality, dementia and mentalize.
intro.cn: mental 是拉丁语 ment-“心智”加形容词词尾 -al。这个后缀在英语里能产；词干 ment- 不能单独成词，却在 mentality、dementia、mentalize 中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin mentalis was built on Latin mens (genitive mentis) 'mind', from PIE *men- 'to think'. The same root supplies dementia (de- 'away' + mens) and the native English mind.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 mentalis 建立在拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）“心智”之上，源自原始印欧语 *men-“思考”。同一词根也给出 dementia（de-“离开”+ mens）以及英语本族词 mind。

items.meaning: of or relating to the mind
items.meaningCN: 心理的；心智的（ment- 心智 + -al 形容词词尾）
items.example: The test measures mental rather than manual speed.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试测的是思维速度，而不是手的速度。

items.meaning: a way of thinking; mental character
items.meaningCN: 心态；思维方式（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The team's mentality changed after the first win.
items.exampleCN: 首胜之后，球队的心态变了。

items.meaning: in the mind; with respect to the mind
items.meaningCN: 心理上；在脑中（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She counted the steps mentally before jumping.
items.exampleCN: 起跳前她在心里数了步子。

items.meaning: a mind-reading performer; a believer in mentalism
items.meaningCN: 读心术表演者；心灵主义者（-ist 指人）
items.example: The mentalist guessed the card without touching it.
items.exampleCN: 那位读心术表演者没碰牌就猜中了。

items.meaning: the view that mind or consciousness is fundamental
items.meaningCN: 心灵主义；唯心论（-ism 表学说）
items.example: Mentalism treats consciousness as the basic stuff of reality.
items.exampleCN: 心灵主义把意识当作现实的基本材料。

items.meaning: relating to mentalism or to explanations in mental terms
items.meaningCN: 心灵主义的；用心理术语解释的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 行为主义者拒斥用心理术语所作的解释。

items.meaning: to understand behaviour as arising from mental states
items.meaningCN: 心智化；把行为理解为心理状态的产物（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: Children learn to mentalize through play.
items.exampleCN: 儿童在游戏中学着理解他人的心理。

items.meaning: a condition in which the mind has gone away
items.meaningCN: 痴呆；认知功能衰退（de- 离开 + ment- 心智 + -ia 状态）
items.example: The early signs of dementia were mistaken for tiredness.
items.exampleCN: 痴呆的早期迹象被误认为是疲劳。

items.meaning: out of one's mind; wildly foolish
items.meaningCN: 精神错乱的；荒唐的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The plan was demented from the first page.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划从第一页起就荒唐透顶。

items.meaning: an object kept as a reminder
items.meaningCN: 纪念物；使人想起某事的物件（源自拉丁语祈使式“记得”）
items.example: He kept the ticket as a memento of the trip.
items.exampleCN: 他把那张票留着，作为那次旅行的纪念。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 失去理智的；精神错乱的

definition_zh: 精神上；心理上；在脑中；智力上
definition_en: in the mind or in thought, rather than in the body, on paper or out loud
core_image: 灯下的人把纸笔都收进抽屉，整道题的步骤全在脑子里走
scene: 深夜的考场里，纸笔都收进了抽屉，几个学生闭着眼，把整道题的步骤在心里重走一遍。She ran the whole route mentally before she set foot on the track.
sceneCN: 这里 mentally 是「在脑中、在心里默想」（第 2 个义项：不写不念地在脑内进行）；句意为她踏上跑道之前，先在脑子里把整条路线走了一遍。

pos.zh: 精神上；心理上；在脑中；智力上

derivatives.zh: mentally 的形容词形式，由拉丁词干 ment- 加 -al 构成，义为「精神的；心理的」
由 mental 加 -ity 构成，义为「心态；思维方式」
由 mental 加 -ism 构成，义为「唯心论；心理主义」

senses.title: In the mind rather than in the body
senses.definition: in a person's mind or thoughts, as opposed to the body or the physical side
senses.definitionCN: 在人的心智或思绪层面，与身体、体力相对
senses.example: He was mentally tired long before his legs gave out.
senses.exampleCN: 他的腿还没垮，人已经在精神上累透了。
senses.why: The adverb is built on the Latin noun for mind, so it always reports what happens inside the head while the limbs may be doing nothing at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词建立在拉丁语中表示心智的名词上，所以它报告的总是脑袋里发生的事，而四肢可能什么都没做。

senses.title: Inside the head, with nothing written or spoken
senses.definition: by thinking or calculating silently, without writing anything down or saying the steps aloud
senses.definitionCN: 在脑子里默想、默算，不写下来，也不把步骤念出声
senses.example: She multiplied the figures mentally and nodded.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那几个数字在心里乘了一遍，然后点了点头。
senses.why: Here the mind is not only where the work happens but the only tool used, so the adverb moves from naming a place to naming a method.
senses.whyCN: 这里脑子不只是事情发生的地点，还是唯一被使用的工具，于是副词从指出地点转为指出方法。

senses.title: In the area of intelligence and reasoning
senses.definition: in the field of thinking and reasoning, especially when a task is measured against physical effort
senses.definitionCN: 在思考与推理的层面，尤用于把一项任务与体力消耗作对比
senses.example: The job is mentally demanding but physically light.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作费脑子，但不太费体力。
senses.why: A mind can be worked as hard as a muscle, so this sense weighs a task by the thinking it takes instead of by the weight it moves.
senses.whyCN: 脑子可以像肌肉一样被使到极限，所以这个义项用耗多少思考来衡量任务，而不是用搬动多少重量。

intro.en: Mentally is an English adverb built from the Latin noun for mind. Its history is short and plain: a Latin stem, a Late Latin adjective, and an English suffix of manner.
intro.cn: mentally 是由拉丁语中表示心智的名词构成的英语副词。它的来历简短而平实：一个拉丁词干、一个晚期拉丁形容词，再加一个英语方式副词词尾。

items.en: Mens, with the stem ment-, was the Latin noun for mind, thought and the power of reasoning.
items.cn: mens 及其词干 ment- 是拉丁语中表示心智、思想与推理能力的名词。

items.en: Mentalis was formed on that stem with a suffix of relation, so it meant belonging to the mind.
items.cn: mentalis 在这个词干上加了表关系的后缀，意为属于心智的。

items.en: English borrowed mental in the medieval period for whatever belonged to the mind, and it was regularly set against bodily.
items.cn: 英语在中古时期借入 mental，指属于心智的一切，并经常与「身体的」相对使用。

items.en: The suffix -ly turned that adjective into an adverb of manner, so the new word answered how something was done, in the mind.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 把这个形容词变成方式副词，新词回答的是「以何种方式」，即「在心里」。

items.en: Modern English applies the adverb to illness, effort, rehearsal and arithmetic, always marking the mind as the place where the action goes on.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个副词用在疾病、努力、预演和算术上，始终把心智标记为动作进行的地点。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem for mind and one word that only resembles it; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs for thinking, feeling and the inner life.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「心智」的拉丁词干展开，另收一个只是形似的词；近义组收表示思考、感受与内心活动的副词。

entries.definition: Of or belonging to the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 属于心智的；精神的。

entries.definition: A settled way of thinking shared by a person or a group.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人或一群人固定的思维方式。

entries.definition: A trusted adviser; it only looks close and comes from a different source.
entries.definitionCN: 值得信赖的指导者；只是拼写与 mental 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: In terms of the working of the mind and emotions.
entries.definitionCN: 从心理与情绪的运作来看。

entries.definition: In terms of reasoning and understanding.
entries.definitionCN: 在推理与理解方面。

entries.definition: In terms of mental processes such as memory and judgement, used in technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 就记忆、判断等心智过程而言，多用于学术文字。

entries.definition: In terms of feeling rather than thought.
entries.definitionCN: 就感受而非思考而言。

normalIntro.en: This adverb is a small machine of three parts, a Latin stem for mind, a Latin ending, and an English ending that makes adverbs.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词是一台三件组成的小机器：表示心智的拉丁词干、一个拉丁词尾，以及一个把词变成副词的英语词尾。

normal.en: Mens is Latin for mind, so mentally always marks the head as the place where something happens.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mens 意为心智，所以 mentally 总是把脑袋标成事情发生的地点。

normal.en: Mental is the adjective and -ly makes it an adverb of manner, so the pair answers what kind and in what way.
normal.cn: mental 是形容词，-ly 把它变成方式副词，于是这一对词一个回答「何种」，一个回答「如何」。

normal.en: Mentality is the noun for a whole settled outlook, while mentally describes a single act of thinking.
normal.cn: mentality 指一整套固定的看法，而 mentally 描述一次具体的思考。

normal.en: Mentally ill and mentally disabled are fixed phrases in medicine and law, where the adverb modifies the state rather than the action.
normal.cn: mentally ill 与 mentally disabled 是医学和法律里的固定说法，副词修饰的是状态而非动作。

normal.en: Mentally demanding weighs a task by thinking, just as physically demanding weighs it by the body.
normal.cn: mentally demanding 用思考量一项任务，正如 physically demanding 用身体来量。

abstract.en: The word quietly insists that a person can be worn out while sitting perfectly still.
abstract.cn: 这个词静静坚持一件事：一个人可以完全坐着不动，却已经被用尽。

abstract.en: A route walked in the head before it is walked on the ground says that rehearsal is a real form of doing.
abstract.cn: 先在心里走一遍、再落到地面上走，说明预演本身就是一种真实的行动。

abstract.en: Because the adverb names only the place, never the content, it can hold grief, arithmetic and memory in one small word.
abstract.cn: 因为这个副词只说出地点、从不说出内容，它才能用小小一个词同时装下悲伤、算术与记忆。

examples.en: He counted the change mentally before handing over the note.
examples.cn: 他把零钱在心里算了一遍，才把纸币递过去。

examples.en: She stayed mentally alert through the whole night shift.
examples.cn: 整个夜班期间，她的头脑一直保持清醒。

examples.en: The course is mentally demanding but easy on the legs.
examples.cn: 这门课很费脑子，但对腿脚没什么负担。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「门特利」——门里特别亮的那盏灯，照的是脑子；记住 mentally 是精神上、在心里。

root: 拉丁语 mens（心智，词干 ment-）→ 晚期拉丁语 mentalis（属于心智的）→ 英语 mental（精神的）+ -ly（方式副词词尾）→ mentally。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the mind as the place where something happens. From there the adverb divides into a state, a silent method, and a measure of how much thinking a task costs.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把心智当作事情发生的地点。副词由此分出三种用法：一种状态、一种不出声的方法，以及衡量任务耗多少思考的尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit desk with the paper pushed aside and all the work going on behind the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯亮着，纸被推到一边，所有活都在眼睛后面进行。

branches.en: a tired face long before tired legs
branches.cn: 人先累在脸上，腿还没累

branches.en: figures moving behind closed eyes
branches.cn: 闭着眼在脑中走过一串数字

branches.en: a desk cleared of paper and pen
branches.cn: 桌上纸笔都收起来了

branches.en: a mind worn out while the body sits still
branches.cn: 身体坐着不动，脑子已经用尽

branches.en: a worker finishing the sum without a single note
branches.cn: 干活的人一张纸都没用就解完了

intro.en: The word is assembled from a Latin noun of mind, a Latin suffix of relation, and an English suffix that turns adjectives into adverbs.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个表示心智的拉丁名词、一个拉丁关系后缀，以及一个把形容词变成副词的英语后缀拼成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 提及；说起；提到的话；嘉奖；更不用说
definition_en: to speak or write about something briefly; also a short reference, a formal naming for praise, or a phrase that adds a stronger point
core_image: 一个人说话时顺手把某件事轻轻带过，只用半句话点到
scene: 会议开到一半，有人问起预算，负责人只在纸上写了一行小字。At the meeting she mentioned the budget only once, then moved on.
sceneCN: 这里是「提到、说起」（第 1 个义项：口头或书面简短提及）；句意为她在会上只提了一次预算，随后就继续往下说。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、纸笔、写着一行小字的便笺。

pos.zh: 提到；说起；点名表扬
提及；提到

derivatives.zh: 由 mention 加 -able 构成，义为「值得一提的」
由 un- 加 mentionable 构成，义为「不宜提及的；说不出口的」
由 afore（在前面）与 mentioned 复合而成，义为「上述的」

senses.title: To refer to something briefly
senses.definition: to say or write something about someone or something, without going into detail
senses.definitionCN: 简短地说到或写到某人或某事，不作详细展开
senses.example: She mentioned your name at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她在会上提到了你的名字。
senses.why: The Latin noun mentio is a calling to mind; to mention something is to bring it into the listener's mind for a moment, not to dwell on it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 mentio 本义是「唤起心中的记忆」；mention 一件事，就是把它在听者心里唤起来一小会儿，而不是停下来细讲。

senses.title: A brief reference
senses.definition: a short remark or written reference to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某事的简短评论或书面提及
senses.example: There was no mention of the price in the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 信里没有提到价格。
senses.why: Once the verb names the act, the noun can name the act itself as a thing: a mention is the small trace the act leaves in speech or text.
senses.whyCN: 动词既然指「提到」这个动作，名词就可以把动作本身当成一件事来指：a mention 就是这一动作在话语或文字里留下的一点小痕迹。

senses.title: To name someone for praise
senses.definition: to name a person formally, especially in a military report, as deserving recognition
senses.definitionCN: 正式点出某人的名字以示表彰，尤指在军方报告中
senses.example: The officer was mentioned in dispatches for his conduct.
senses.exampleCN: 这名军官因表现突出在战报中受到嘉奖。
senses.why: A formal report lists names one by one; naming a person in that list is a kind of mention, so the word comes to mean official recognition.
senses.whyCN: 正式报告会逐个列出名字；把某人写进这份名单，本身就是一种 mention，于是这个词引申为官方表彰。

senses.title: An added point that strengthens the statement
senses.definition: used to introduce a further fact that makes what has just been said stronger
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出更进一步的事实，使刚说过的话更有分量
senses.example: He speaks three languages, not to mention his fluent Chinese.
senses.exampleCN: 他会说三种语言，更不用说他那口流利的中文了。
senses.why: The phrase not to mention began as a way of saying 'without even speaking of', and it turned a bare mention into a rhetorical upgrade.
senses.whyCN: 短语 not to mention 起初表示「连说都不用说」，于是把一个轻描淡写的提及变成了加强语气的修辞手段。

intro.en: Mention comes from a Latin noun for calling something to mind, and its history keeps the idea of the mind rather than the mouth.
intro.cn: mention 来自拉丁语中表示「把某事唤到心上」的名词，它的历史始终围绕「心」而不是「嘴」。

items.en: Mentio meant a mentioning or a calling to mind, and it was formed on the root of mens, the mind.
items.cn: mentio 意为「提及、唤到心上」，由表示「心」的 mens 词根构成。

items.en: Mens named the mind or the thinking faculty; the same root produced memini, I remember, and memor, mindful.
items.cn: mens 指心智或思考能力；同一词根还产生 memini（我记得）与 memor（记着的）。

items.en: Old French took the Latin noun as mention and used it for a spoken or written reference.
items.cn: 古法语把这一拉丁名词写作 mention，用于口头或书面的提及。

items.en: Middle English used mention as both noun and verb, and the verb soon became the everyday way to point at a topic.
items.cn: 中古英语中 mention 既作名词也作动词，动词很快成为点出一个话题的日常说法。

items.en: Modern English fixed the phrase not to mention and the military sense of being mentioned in dispatches.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了 not to mention 这一说法，以及「在战报中受到嘉奖」的军事义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that share the Latin mind-root or merely resemble the spelling; the near-meaning group collects verbs for pointing at a topic.
note.cn: 形近组收共享拉丁「心」词根或只是拼写相像的词；近义组收表示「点出话题」的动词。

entries.definition: A remark that gives an opinion; it shares the ending but comes from Latin commentum, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 发表意见的评论；它与 mention 只是词尾相像，词源来自拉丁语 commentum，并非同根。

entries.definition: Relating to the mind; built on the same Latin root mens.
entries.definitionCN: 与心智有关的；建立在同一拉丁词根 mens 上。

entries.definition: A trusted adviser; the word goes back to the Greek name Mentor, not to the Latin mind-root.
entries.definitionCN: 可信赖的顾问；源自希腊人名 Mentor，与拉丁「心」词根无关，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A very short period of time; from Latin momentum, a movement or instant, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间；来自拉丁语 momentum（运动、瞬间），词源不同，仅拼写相近。

entries.definition: To speak about someone or something briefly.
entries.definitionCN: 简短地谈到某人或某事。

entries.definition: To mention something as an example or support.
entries.definitionCN: 举例或引证时提到某事。

entries.definition: To refer to something indirectly rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 间接地提及某事，而不直接点明。

entries.definition: To remark on something in speech or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 在口头或书面中谈到某事。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin noun for memory and a root for mind; its family keeps speaking tied to thinking.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示记忆的拉丁名词与表示心智的词根上，同族词始终把「说」和「想」系在一起。

normal.en: Mentio in Latin is a calling to mind, so a mention brings a topic into the listener's head rather than into the centre of the talk.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mentio 是「唤到心上」，所以 mention 是把话题送进听者脑中，而不是摆到谈话中心。

normal.en: The root mens means mind, and mental still carries that meaning, which is why a mention is a mental event before it is a spoken one.
normal.cn: 词根 mens 意为心智，mental 至今保留此义，所以 mention 先是心里的事，然后才是嘴里的事。

normal.en: Mentioned in dispatches is a fixed military phrase: the name is written into a report, and writing a name is a literal mention.
normal.cn: mentioned in dispatches 是固定的军事说法：名字被写进报告，而写下一个名字就是字面意义上的 mention。

normal.en: Not to mention works like a hinge: it adds a stronger fact after a weaker one.
normal.cn: not to mention 像一扇铰链：先给一个较轻的事实，再挂上一个更重的。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one spelling, so mention can be the act or the short reference it produces.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，所以 mention 既可以是「提到」这个动作，也可以是动作留下的那句短话。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tapping one word on a long page and then moving on; that tap is a mention.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在长页面上轻点一个词，然后继续移动；那一点就是 mention。

abstract.en: A mention is a small door: it lets a topic in without letting it take over the room.
abstract.cn: mention 是一扇小门：它让话题进来，却不让话题占满整个房间。

abstract.en: The word ties speech to memory, because what is mentioned is meant to stay in the mind afterwards.
abstract.cn: 这个词把说话和记忆系在一起，因为被提到的东西本来就是为了留在心里。

examples.en: She mentioned your name at the meeting.
examples.cn: 她在会上提到了你的名字。

examples.en: There was no mention of the price in the letter.
examples.cn: 信里没有提到价格。

examples.en: He speaks three languages, not to mention his fluent Chinese.
examples.cn: 他会说三种语言，更不用说他那口流利的中文了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「门神」——进门先看见门神，忍不住提一句；mention 意为提及。

root: 拉丁语 mentio（提及）来自 mens（心智）的词根 ment-；同族词多与「想、记、心」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a brief bringing-to-mind; it splits into the spoken reference, the formal naming for praise, and the phrase that adds a stronger point.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「把某事唤到心上的一提」；由此分出那句简短的提及、为表彰而点名的提及，以及用来加强语气的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger tapping one word on a page and then moving on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指在页面上轻点一个词，随即移开。

branches.en: a speaker touching a topic and moving on
branches.cn: 说话人碰一下话题就继续往下

branches.en: a short line in a letter that keeps a topic alive
branches.cn: 信里短短一行字，让一个话题留在心上

branches.en: a name written into a military report
branches.cn: 名字被写进一份军方报告

branches.en: a hinge adding a heavier fact to a light one
branches.cn: 铰链一般，把更重的事实挂到轻的话后面

branches.en: the same small trace seen as act and as thing
branches.cn: 同一点小痕迹，既可以看作动作，也可以看作留下的东西

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin noun of memory, the root for mind, and two English suffixes that make it a quality or a possibility.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示记忆的拉丁名词、表示心智的词根，以及两个把它变成「性质」和「可能性」的英语后缀支撑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun mentio and the mind-root mens supply the core; English suffixes build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 mentio 与表示心智的词根 mens 提供核心，其余由英语后缀构成。

items.meaning: a mentioning, a calling to mind
to think, to have in mind

items.meaningCN: 名词后缀：行为、状态或结果

latinEntries.meaning: a mentioning, a calling to mind

definition_zh: 菜单；菜谱；（电脑）菜单；选项列表
definition_en: a list of dishes served in a restaurant, or a list of choices shown on a screen or offered by a service
core_image: 一张折起的纸，上面一行行写着今天能点的菜
scene: 餐馆门口的木架上夹着一张纸，客人进门先低头看它。At the counter, the waiter handed us a menu with today's specials.
sceneCN: 这里是「菜单」（第 1 个义项：餐馆里列出菜品的单子）；句意为在柜台边，服务员递给我们一张写着当日特色菜的菜单。图中可辨识物件：木架、夹子、折起的纸单。

pos.zh: 菜单；菜谱；（电脑）菜单；选项列表

derivatives.zh: 由 sub-（下、次级）加 menu 构成，义为「子菜单」
由 menu 与 driven 复合而成，义为「菜单驱动的」
由 menu 与 bar 复合而成，义为「菜单栏」

senses.title: A list of dishes in a restaurant
senses.definition: a list of the food that a restaurant can serve, often with prices
senses.definitionCN: 餐馆可供应的食物清单，通常附价格
senses.example: The menu changes with the season.
senses.exampleCN: 菜单随季节更换。
senses.why: The French word first meant a small, detailed list; a restaurant's bill of fare is exactly such a detailed list, so the label stuck to food.
senses.whyCN: 这个法语词最初指「细小而详细的清单」；餐馆的菜品单正是一份这样的详细清单，于是这个称呼就落到了食物上。

senses.title: A list of choices on a computer screen
senses.definition: a list of commands or choices that appears on a screen and can be selected
senses.definitionCN: 出现在屏幕上、可供选择的命令或选项列表
senses.example: Open the file menu and choose save.
senses.exampleCN: 打开文件菜单，选择保存。
senses.why: A screen menu is a list of what you may pick, which is the same shape as a bill of fare: many items, one choice.
senses.whyCN: 屏幕菜单是一份「你可以挑什么」的清单，形状和菜品单一样：很多项目，只选一个。

senses.title: A range of services or options offered
senses.definition: the set of services or possibilities that an organization makes available
senses.definitionCN: 某个机构所能提供的一整套服务或可能性
senses.example: The clinic offers a wide menu of treatments.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所提供种类繁多的治疗方案。
senses.why: Once menu means a list to choose from, it can leave the restaurant and describe any organized set of options, such as treatments or courses.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 menu 表示「供人挑选的清单」，它就能离开餐馆，去描述任何被整理好的选项集合，例如治疗方案或课程。

intro.en: Menu is a French word for something small and detailed; the restaurant sense grew out of the idea of a finely itemized list.
intro.cn: menu 是法语中表示「细小而详细」的词；餐馆义正是从「分得很细的清单」这个想法长出来的。

items.en: Minutus, the past participle of minuere, meant made small or minute, and it is the source of the French adjective.
items.cn: minutus 是 minuere 的过去分词，意为「被弄小的、微小的」，是法语形容词的来源。

items.en: Minuere meant to lessen or make smaller, and its root min- still marks words about smallness.
items.cn: minuere 意为「减少、使变小」，它的词根 min- 至今标记着与「小」有关的词。

items.en: French menu was an adjective meaning small, fine or detailed, and a menu could be a detailed list written in small writing.
items.cn: 法语 menu 是形容词，意为「小的、精细的、详细的」，而一份 menu 可以是用小字写成的详细清单。

items.en: English borrowed menu in the eighteenth century for a bill of fare, at first as a somewhat fashionable French term.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 menu 指菜品单，起初还带点法语时髦词的意味。

items.en: Modern English extended the word to lists of commands on a screen and, by analogy, to any organized set of choices.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词扩展到屏幕上的命令列表，并类推到任何整理好的选择集合。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin root for small or merely similar in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers other words for a list of choices.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁「小」词根上、或只是拼写相像的词；近义组收其他表示「选择清单」的词。

entries.definition: Very small; from Latin minutus, the same root as menu.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的；来自拉丁语 minutus，与 menu 同根。

entries.definition: A slow elegant dance; its French name goes back to menu, small, because of its small steps.
entries.definitionCN: 一种缓慢优雅的舞蹈；其法语名称可追溯到 menu（小的），因舞步细碎。

entries.definition: The smallest possible amount; built on Latin minimus, from the same root as minuere.
entries.definitionCN: 可能的最小量；建立在拉丁语 minimus 上，与 minuere 同根。

entries.definition: A book of instructions; from Latin manus, hand, so only the spelling resembles menu.
entries.definitionCN: 说明书；来自拉丁语 manus（手），只是拼写与 menu 相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: An old phrase for a menu, listing the dishes and their prices.
entries.definitionCN: menu 的旧说法，列出菜品与价格。

entries.definition: A series of items written or printed one after another.
entries.definitionCN: 一条条写出或印出的项目。

entries.definition: A complete list of things, often arranged in order.
entries.definitionCN: 常按顺序排列的完整清单。

entries.definition: A group of things from which one may choose.
entries.definitionCN: 可供从中挑选的一组东西。

normalIntro.en: The word began as an adjective for small, fine detail and ends as a name for any list you pick from.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从表示「细小、精细」的形容词出发，最后成了任何「供你挑选的清单」的名字。

normal.en: Minutus in Latin means made small, so a menu is literally a list written out in small, fine detail.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 minutus 意为「被弄小的」，所以 menu 字面上就是一份写得细小而详细的清单。

normal.en: The min- root in minimum and minute marks smallness, and menu belongs to that same family.
normal.cn: minimum 与 minute 里的 min- 词根标记「小」，menu 属于同一族。

normal.en: A restaurant menu and a computer menu are both lists of things you may choose, which is why one word serves both.
normal.cn: 餐馆菜单和电脑菜单都是「你可以挑什么」的清单，所以一个词身兼两用。

normal.en: Menu bar and drop-down menu are compounds: the second word tells you where or how the list appears.
normal.cn: menu bar 与 drop-down menu 都是复合词，后一个词说明清单出现在哪里、以何种方式出现。

normal.en: Menu of services shows the word escaping the restaurant: any organized set of options can be a menu.
normal.cn: menu of services 显示这个词已经离开餐馆：任何整理好的选项集合都可以叫 menu。

abstract.en: Think of a folded card by the door: it lists what the house can offer before you even sit down.
abstract.cn: 想象门口一张折起的卡片：你还没坐下，它就把这家店能提供什么列给你看。

abstract.en: A menu is a map of choices, not the meal itself; it promises without feeding you.
abstract.cn: menu 是一张选择的地图，不是饭本身；它作出承诺，却不喂饱你。

abstract.en: The same word on a screen reminds us that a list of options is now the shape of modern work.
abstract.cn: 同一个词出现在屏幕上，提醒我们：选项清单已经成了现代工作的形状。

examples.en: The menu changes with the season.
examples.cn: 菜单随季节更换。

examples.en: Open the file menu and choose save.
examples.cn: 打开文件菜单，选择保存。

examples.en: The clinic offers a wide menu of treatments.
examples.cn: 这家诊所提供种类繁多的治疗方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没牛」——菜单上写着没有牛肉，顾客只好换一道；menu 是菜单。

root: 法语 menu（细小、详细）来自拉丁语 minutus（微小的），词根 min- 表示「小」；同族词多与「小、减少」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a detailed list to choose from; it divides into the restaurant list, the screen list, and any organized set of services.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一份供人挑选的详细清单；它分出餐馆菜品单、屏幕选项单，以及任何整理好的服务方案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded card by the door listing, line by line, what can be ordered.
core.cn: 核心意象：门口一张折起的卡片，一行行写着今天能点什么。

branches.en: a folded card clipped to a stand by the door
branches.cn: 夹在门口架子上的折页

branches.en: a line of dishes with prices beside them
branches.cn: 一行行菜品，旁边标着价格

branches.en: a list dropping down from the top of a screen
branches.cn: 从屏幕顶部垂下来的列表

branches.en: a clinic handing out a sheet of treatments
branches.cn: 诊所递出一张写满治疗项目的单子

branches.en: one shape of choosing, two places to choose from
branches.cn: 同一种挑选的形状，出现在两个地方

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin adjective of smallness and its verb, then turned into an English noun that now names any list of choices.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「小」的拉丁形容词及其动词构成，后来变成英语名词，如今指任何选择清单。

latinIntro.en: A Latin adjective of smallness and its verb lead to the French word, which English then took over.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「小」的拉丁形容词及其动词导向法语词形，英语再整体借入。

definition_zh: 商人；（批发的）货商；酒商、煤炭商等专营商人；商船的
definition_en: a person or firm that buys and sells goods, especially in large quantities or across borders
core_image: 码头仓库门口，一个穿长外套的人对着账本清点整匹的布，身后是刚卸下的货堆
scene: 码头仓库里，收货人掀开帆布，逐匹检查刚卸下的丝绸，账本上记着欠款与运费。The merchant sold silk by the bale and never dealt in single bolts.
sceneCN: 这里 merchant 指「以大宗货物跨地买卖为业的人」（第 1 个义项：作为从事大宗贸易的商人）；句意为这位商人按整包卖丝绸，从不拆成单匹零售；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 商人；批发商；专营商人
商船的；商业的（多见于 merchant ship、merchant navy）

derivatives.zh: merchant + -ise（名词后缀）→ 商品；推销（语义偏移：从人转到货）
merchandise + -ing（动名词）→ 货品推广与陈列
merchant + -able（可…的）→ 适销的（法律用语）
merchant + man → 商船（语义偏移：从人转到船）
意大利 mercante + -ile → 贸易的；重商的
com- + merx → 商业（同根，走抽象活动那条线）

senses.title: Trader in goods, especially wholesale
senses.titleCN: 从事货物买卖的商人（尤指批发）
senses.definition: a person or firm that buys goods in quantity and sells them on, often across distance
senses.definitionCN: 成批买进再转售的个人或企业，常跨距离经营
senses.example: The merchant sold silk by the bale and never dealt in single bolts.
senses.exampleCN: 这位商人按整包卖丝绸，从不拆成单匹零售。
senses.why: Latin mercari 'to trade' plus the person suffix -ant gives the one who trades, and the word keeps the bulk-dealing sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 mercari「做买卖」加人称后缀 -ant 给出「做买卖的人」，而这个词保留了成批交易之义。

senses.title: A shopkeeper, in older British use
senses.definition: dated: a retail shopkeeper, especially one who owns the shop
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：零售店主，尤指店铺所有者
senses.example: The village merchant knew every family's account by heart.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的店主把每家的账都记在心里。
senses.why: Before chain stores, the local shopkeeper was simply the person who traded, so the word needed no qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 在连锁店出现之前，本地店主就是做买卖的那个人，因此这个词无需限定语。

senses.title: Dealer in one commodity
senses.titleCN: 某一类货品的专营商人
senses.definition: a specialist dealer whose trade is named with the word, as a wine merchant or coal merchant
senses.definitionCN: 以本词构成称谓的专营商人，如酒商、煤商
senses.example: The wine merchant will not open a bottle that has not rested a year.
senses.exampleCN: 那位酒商不肯开一瓶还没放满一年的酒。
senses.why: The compound pattern merchant of X narrows the general trader to one stock.
senses.whyCN: 「X + merchant」这一复合模式把一般商人收窄到一种货品。

senses.title: Wholesaler supplying retailers
senses.titleCN: 向零售商供货的批发商
senses.definition: a middle trader who buys from producers and supplies shops rather than end customers
senses.definitionCN: 从生产者买进、供给店铺而非最终顾客的中间商
senses.example: Retailers complained that the merchant kept the best lots for himself.
senses.exampleCN: 零售商抱怨那位批发商把最好的货留给了自己。
senses.why: Scale separates the merchant from the shop: one moves cases, the other sells units.
senses.whyCN: 规模把 merchant 与店铺分开：一个搬整箱，一个卖单件。

senses.title: Member of a chartered trading company
senses.definition: historical: a member of a company granted a monopoly of trade with a region
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法：获得某地区贸易垄断权的公司成员
senses.example: A merchant of the company could lose his charter for private dealing.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司的商人若私自交易，会被吊销特许状。
senses.why: Charters turned merchants into licensed agents of a state, and the word absorbed that status.
senses.whyCN: 特许状把商人变成国家的受许代理人，这个词也就吸收了那层身份。

senses.title: One who trades in something abstract
senses.titleCN: 经营抽象之物的人（比喻）
senses.definition: figuratively, a person who circulates a quality or a commodity that is not goods, as a merchant of doubt
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指流通某种非货物之物的人，如散布疑虑者
senses.example: He is a merchant of doubt, paid by the column and never by the fact.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个贩卖疑虑的人，按专栏收钱，从不按事实收钱。
senses.why: If goods can be sold, anything marketable can be sold, so the person noun travels with them.
senses.whyCN: 既然货物能卖，任何可售之物都能卖，指人的名词便随之而去。

senses.title: Attributive use for shipping
senses.definition: used before nouns to mark vessels or fleets that carry commercial cargo rather than troops
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，标出载运商业货物而非军队的船只或船队
senses.example: The merchant fleet was requisitioned before the war began.
senses.exampleCN: 战争开始前，商船队就被征用了。
senses.why: A trader on land becomes a ship at sea, and the noun works as a plain classifier.
senses.whyCN: 陆上的商人在海上成了船，这个名词便充当简单的分类语。

senses.title: Promoter of something unwelcome
senses.titleCN: 推销不受欢迎之物的人
senses.definition: in modern compounds, a person who promotes a bad thing as if selling it, as a doom merchant
senses.definitionCN: 在现代复合词中，指把坏东西当作货品来推销的人，如唱衰者
senses.example: The paper calls every forecaster a doom merchant.
senses.exampleCN: 这家报纸把每个预测者都叫作唱衰者。
senses.why: The selling frame is so strong that it can be attached to ideas nobody wants to buy.
senses.whyCN: 兜售这一框架太强，以至于可以挂到没人想买的主张上。

intro.en: Merchant is the person-shaped member of the goods family: the same Latin noun for merchandise, put through a verb of trading and a French suffix for people.
intro.cn: merchant 是「货物」词族中取人形的那个成员：同一个表商品的拉丁名词，经一个表交易的动词与一个法语人称后缀而成。

items.en: Merx, genitive mercis, meant 'merchandise, goods'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the links sometimes proposed to a trading root are hypotheses, not established derivations.
items.cn: merx（属格 mercis）意为「货物、商品」。其更深来源不确定；有人提出的与某个交易词根的联系只是假说，并非已成立的派生。

items.en: Mercari 'to trade, to deal' is the deponent verb built on merx; it supplies the stem that carries the person suffix.
items.cn: mercari「做买卖、交易」是建于 merx 之上的异态动词，提供了承载人称后缀的词干。

items.en: Mercator 'trader' is the direct Latin person noun, and it survives in English in learned and historical writing.
items.cn: mercator「商人」是直接的拉丁人称名词，在英语的学术与历史写作中仍可见到。

items.en: Old French marchant names a trader or shopkeeper and is the form English borrowed, with the -ch- that English later reduced.
items.cn: 古法语 marchant 指商人或店主，是英语借入的形式，其中的 -ch- 后来在英语里弱化。

items.en: Early English spellings vary between marchaunt and merchant; the word covers both the long-distance trader and the local shopkeeper.
items.cn: 早期英语拼写在 marchaunt 与 merchant 之间摆动；这个词同时涵盖长途商人与本地店主。

items.en: Modern English separates merchant from shopkeeper and keeps the word for wholesale, specialist and shipping uses; the compound patterns wine merchant and doom merchant show both ends of that range.
items.cn: 现代英语把 merchant 与店主分开，保留批发、专营与航运用法；wine merchant 与 doom merchant 这两个复合模式正显出这一区间的两端。

note.en: The first group shares the goods root or the shape; the second holds words for the people who sell at different points in the chain.
note.cn: 第一组共享货物词根或外形；第二组是销售链条不同环节上的人。

entries.definition: The noun for goods bought and sold, formed from merchant; it names the cargo, not the trader.
entries.definitionCN: 指买卖的货物，由 merchant 构成；它指货，不指人。

entries.definition: Describing trade or a policy bent on profit; it came through Italian and has no plural or person form.
entries.definitionCN: 描述贸易或唯利是图的政策；经意大利语而来，无人称或复数形式。

entries.definition: A commercial-law word meaning fit to be sold, said of goods rather than of people.
entries.definitionCN: 商法用词，意为适销，说的是货物而非人。

entries.definition: The abstract noun of trade; merchant is the person who carries it on.
entries.definitionCN: 指贸易的抽象名词；merchant 是从事贸易的人。

entries.definition: Anyone who trades, including a market stall or a brokerage desk; merchant sounds older and grander.
entries.definitionCN: 任何做交易的人，包括市场摊位或经纪台；merchant 显得更老派、更有分量。

entries.definition: A specialist buyer and seller, as a car dealer or an art dealer; merchant often implies bulk and distance.
entries.definitionCN: 某一商品或市场的专营买卖者，如汽车经销商、艺术品经销商；merchant 常含大宗与跨地之意。

entries.definition: A trader who sells to shops rather than to households; the word names a position, not a tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 卖给店铺而非住户的商人；这个词标出链条位置，而非一种传统。

entries.definition: The person behind a shop counter; it fixes the word to one premises, which merchant never does.
entries.definitionCN: 站在店铺柜台后的人；它把人固定在某一处店面，而 merchant 从不这样限定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: merx 'goods' + -ant 'person': the person of goods.
normal.cn: merx「货物」+ -ant「人」：货物的人。

normal.en: The family runs merchant, merchandise, merchandising, merchantable, merchantman, mercantile, commerce.
normal.cn: 同族词有 merchant、merchandise、merchandising、merchantable、merchantman、mercantile、commerce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark specialities: wine merchant, coal merchant, merchant bank, merchant ship.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出专营：酒商、煤商、商人银行、商船。

normal.en: The word moved from person to cargo: merchant sells merchandise.
normal.cn: 这个词从人走到货：merchant 卖 merchandise。

normal.en: Merchantman is a ship, not a man, a reminder that the suffix once meant a vessel.
normal.cn: merchantman 是船而非人，提醒人们这个后缀曾指船只。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger in which every page is a debt and every debt is a bale of cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账册，每一页是一笔欠款，每笔欠款是一包布。

abstract.en: Picture a charter that turns a private trader into an arm of the state.
abstract.cn: 想象一份特许状，把私人商人变成国家的一只手臂。

abstract.en: Picture a newspaper column written by someone who sells fear by the word.
abstract.cn: 想象一个按字出售恐惧的人所写的报纸专栏。

examples.en: A merchant from Genoa financed the voyage and took a third of the cargo.
examples.cn: 一位热那亚商人资助了这次航行，并取走三分之一的货。

examples.en: The coal merchant delivers on Wednesdays and will not come for a single sack.
examples.cn: 煤商每周三送货，不会为一袋煤专门跑一趟。

examples.en: Merchant ships were stopped and searched for contraband.
examples.cn: 商船被拦下搜查违禁品。

dict_mnemonic.text: merce（货物）＋ ant（人）＝ 管货物的人；记「整包进、整包出，账本不离手」。

root: 拉丁 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」→ mercari「做买卖」→ 拉丁 mercator「商人」→ 古法语 marchant → 英语 merchant；merx 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one trader through the chain: bulk dealer, local shopkeeper, single-commodity specialist, wholesaler, chartered agent, dealer in abstractions, shipping classifier, and promoter of bad news.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个商人沿链条走一遍：大宗商、本地店主、单一货品专营者、批发商、受特许的代理人、抽象之物的经营者、航运的分类语，以及坏消息的推销者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger, a bale and a long walk between the quay and the shop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本账册、一包货，以及码头与店铺之间那段长路。

branches.en: BULK AND COUNTER: the same trader scaled down to a village shop before chain stores existed.
branches.cn: 大宗与柜台：同一个商人在连锁店出现之前缩小为村里的店铺。

branches.en: SPECIALITY AND POSITION: one stock only, and a place in the chain between maker and shop.
branches.cn: 专营与位置：只做一种货，并在制作者与店铺之间占一个环节。

branches.en: LICENSED TRADER: a charter converts private dealing into a granted monopoly.
branches.cn: 受许商人：特许状把私人交易转为授予的垄断。

branches.en: ANYTHING SELLABLE: doubt and doom can be stocked and sold like cloth.
branches.cn: 任何可售之物：疑虑与唱衰也能像布匹一样囤积出售。

branches.en: OUTWARD FORMS: at sea the trader becomes a ship, in print a seller of bad news.
branches.cn: 外在形态：在海上商人成船，在纸面上成为坏消息的售卖者。

intro.en: Merchant is a Latin goods noun plus a Latin person suffix, filtered through French; the same root builds the words for goods, for trade policy and for the market itself.
intro.cn: merchant 是一个拉丁货物名词加一个拉丁人称后缀，经法语过滤而成；同一词根还构成指商品、指贸易政策与指市场本身的词。

latinIntro.en: From merx come mercari 'to trade', mercator 'trader', mercatus 'market' and commercium 'trade together'; English draws merchant, merchandise and commerce from that single stock.
latinIntro.cn: 由 merx 生出 mercari「交易」、mercator「商人」、mercatus「市场」与 commercium「共同交易」；英语从这一处取来 merchant、merchandise 与 commerce。

items.example: The root names what is traded.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被交易的东西。

items.example: The verb supplies the stem before the person suffix.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词在人称后缀之前提供词干。

items.example: The person form is the everyday English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个人体形式就是日常英语中的这个词。

items.example: The suffix returns the word to the cargo.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词带回货物。

items.example: The form names the selling work around the goods.
items.exampleCN: 这个形式指围绕货品的销售工作。

items.example: The suffix creates a legal standard for goods.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀为货物造出一条法律标准。

items.example: Here man means vessel, not person.
items.exampleCN: 此处 man 指船只，不指人。

items.example: The Italian route gives a separate adjective.
items.exampleCN: 意大利语这条路径给出另一个形容词。

items.example: The abstract member of the family.
The same stock names where the dealing happens.
items.exampleCN: 同一词源指交易发生之处。

latinEntries.structure: mercari, mercatus sum (verb, first conjugation, deponent)

definition_zh: 仁慈；怜悯；宽恕；宽大处理；幸事
definition_en: kindness shown to someone who could be punished or harmed, the act of forgiving, or a fortunate relief
core_image: 一只本可以落下的手，停在半空，改成了轻轻扶一把
scene: 法庭上，受害者家属沉默许久，最后没有要求最重的刑罚。The judge showed mercy and gave the young man a suspended sentence.
sceneCN: 这里是「仁慈、宽恕」（第 1 个义项：对有权惩罚的人手下留情）；句意为法官动了仁慈之心，判这个年轻人缓刑。图中可辨识物件：法庭木栏、卷宗、法官席。

pos.zh: 仁慈；怜悯；宽恕；宽大处理；幸事

derivatives.zh: 由 mercy 去 y 加 -ful 构成，义为「仁慈的；慈悲的」
由 mercy 去 y 加 -less 构成，义为「无情的；残忍的」
由 merciful 加 -ly 构成，义为「仁慈地；幸好」

senses.title: Compassion toward someone in your power
senses.definition: kindness and forgiveness shown to someone you have the power to punish or harm
senses.definitionCN: 对你本可以惩罚或伤害的人所表现的善意与宽容
senses.example: The judge showed mercy and reduced the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 法官动了仁慈之心，减轻了刑罚。
senses.why: The Latin word first meant a reward or a price paid; Christian writers used it for the unearned favour God gives, and that idea of a gift nobody earned became human compassion.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词最初指「报酬、代价」；基督教作者用它表示上帝白白赐下的恩惠，而「不配得却得到的礼物」这一想法，后来变成了人对人的怜悯。

senses.title: Forgiveness instead of punishment
senses.definition: the act of forgiving an offender or treating them less severely than the rules allow
senses.definitionCN: 原谅犯错者，或对其处理得比规定更宽大
senses.example: She begged the court for mercy.
senses.exampleCN: 她向法庭求情，请求宽恕。
senses.why: Once mercy is a favour granted rather than earned, it naturally appears in courts, where the powerful can choose to relax the full weight of the law.
senses.whyCN: 既然 mercy 是不配得而得到的恩惠，它自然出现在法庭上——掌权者可以选择减轻法律的全力压迫。

senses.title: A fortunate relief
senses.definition: a welcome event that brings relief from pain or difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 带来解脱、令人庆幸的事，使人脱离痛苦或困境
senses.example: It was a mercy that the fever broke before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 烧在黎明前退了，真是件幸事。
senses.why: If mercy is kindness that spares someone, an event that spares us suffering can be called a mercy too, as if the world had chosen to be kind.
senses.whyCN: 如果 mercy 是「手下留情」的善意，那么一件让我们免受痛苦的事也能叫 mercy，就好像这个世界选择对我们仁慈了一回。

senses.title: Completely in someone's power
senses.definition: used in the phrase at the mercy of, meaning completely controlled by another person or force
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 at the mercy of，意为完全受某人或某种力量支配
senses.example: The small boat was at the mercy of the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 小船只能任凭风摆布。
senses.why: To be at someone's mercy is to stand where their kindness or cruelty decides your fate, so the phrase pictures a person wholly handed over to another's will.
senses.whyCN: at someone's mercy 就是站在「对方的仁慈或残忍决定你命运」的位置上，这个短语画出一个人被完全交到别人意志里的样子。

intro.en: Mercy goes back to a Latin word for wages and price, and its move from payment to pardon is one of the most striking shifts in English.
intro.cn: mercy 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「报酬、代价」的词，它从「付钱」转向「宽恕」，是英语里最引人注目的词义变化之一。

items.en: Merces meant pay, wages or a price, the reward owed for work or for a service.
items.cn: merces 意为报酬、工资或代价，即为工作或服务应付的回报。

items.en: Christian writers used merces for the free favour and pardon given by God, a gift not earned by the receiver.
items.cn: 基督教作者用 merces 表示上帝白白赐予的恩惠与赦免，是接受者并未挣得的礼物。

items.en: Old French merci carried the sense of pity and mercy, and also served as a word of thanks.
items.cn: 古法语 merci 带有怜悯与仁慈的意思，同时也用作道谢之词。

items.en: Middle English mercy named both the virtue of compassion and the act of sparing an offender.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mercy 既指仁慈这种德性，也指饶恕犯错者的行为。

items.en: Modern English keeps the courtly and religious senses and adds the everyday phrase at the mercy of.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了法庭与宗教两方面的含义，又增添了日常短语 at the mercy of。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the Latin root for trade and reward; the near-meaning group gathers words for compassion and forgiveness.
note.cn: 形近组收来自拉丁语「交易、报酬」词根的词；近义组收表示怜悯与宽恕的词。

entries.definition: A soldier who fights for pay; from Latin mercenarius, from merces, wages.
entries.definitionCN: 为报酬而战的士兵；来自拉丁语 mercenarius，源出 merces（报酬）。

entries.definition: A person who buys and sells goods; from Latin mercari, to trade, from merx, merchandise.
entries.definitionCN: 买卖货物的人；来自拉丁语 mercari（做买卖），源出 merx（货物）。

entries.definition: Goods for sale; built on the Latin root merc-, trade.
entries.definitionCN: 待售的商品；建立在表示「交易」的拉丁词根 merc- 上。

entries.definition: Relating to trade and commerce; from the same Latin trading root.
entries.definitionCN: 与贸易、商业有关的；来自同一拉丁「交易」词根。

entries.definition: Sympathy for the suffering of others, with a wish to help.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人苦难的同情，并希望帮上一把。

entries.definition: A feeling of sorrow for someone's misfortune.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人不幸的难过之情。

entries.definition: The act of pardoning someone who has done wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 原谅犯错者的行为。

entries.definition: The quality of punishing less severely than allowed.
entries.definitionCN: 处罚比规定更宽大的做法。

normalIntro.en: The word moved from a price paid to a pardon given, and its family keeps the twin ideas of earning and giving.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「付出的代价」走向「给予的宽恕」，它的同族词则一直保留「挣得」与「给予」两条线索。

normal.en: Merces in Latin is wages or a price, so mercy begins in the world of payment and debt.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 merces 是工资或代价，所以 mercy 最初属于「付钱与欠债」的世界。

normal.en: Christian Latin turned the word into God's free pardon, a gift the receiver could never earn.
normal.cn: 基督教拉丁语把这个词转为上帝白白的赦免，是接受者永远挣不到的礼物。

normal.en: Merchant and merchandise keep the trading sense of the same root, which is why they look and sound like mercy.
normal.cn: merchant 与 merchandise 保留同一词根的交易义，所以它们看起来、听起来都像 mercy。

normal.en: Merciful adds -ful to mercy, meaning full of mercy; merciless adds -less, meaning without it.
normal.cn: merciful 在 mercy 后加 -ful，意为「充满仁慈」；merciless 加 -less，意为「没有仁慈」。

normal.en: At the mercy of is a fixed phrase: the person stands exactly where another's kindness decides what happens.
normal.cn: at the mercy of 是固定短语：这个人就站在「别人的仁慈决定结果」的位置上。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand that stops halfway down and turns into a hand that lifts someone up.
abstract.cn: 想象一只已经抬起、准备落下的手，在半空停住，变成一只把人扶起的手。

abstract.en: Mercy is power that chooses not to spend itself.
abstract.cn: mercy 是选择不把力量全部用出去的力量。

abstract.en: A price and a pardon in one word reminds us that forgiving always costs someone something.
abstract.cn: 「代价」与「赦免」同处一词，提醒人：宽恕总要有人付出点什么。

examples.en: The judge showed mercy and reduced the sentence.
examples.cn: 法官动了仁慈之心，减轻了刑罚。

examples.en: She begged the court for mercy.
examples.cn: 她向法庭求情，请求宽恕。

examples.en: The small boat was at the mercy of the wind.
examples.cn: 小船只能任凭风摆布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没事」——本来要重罚，结果说没事；mercy 就是宽恕。

root: 拉丁语 merces（报酬、代价）经基督教拉丁语转为「上帝的恩惠」，再经古法语 merci（怜悯）进入英语；同族词多与交易、报酬有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is kindness that spares; it branches into courtroom forgiveness, fortunate relief, and the phrase for being wholly in another's power.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「手下留情的善意」；由此分出法庭上的宽恕、令人庆幸的解脱，以及表示完全受制于人的短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that could strike, held back and turned into a hand that lifts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只本可以打下去的手，收住了，变成一只扶人的手。

branches.en: a judgement seat where the heavier sentence is set aside
branches.cn: 审判席上，较重的刑罚被放到一边

branches.en: a court where the rules are deliberately softened
branches.cn: 法庭上有意把规矩放松一些

branches.en: a fever breaking before dawn
branches.cn: 烧在黎明前退了下去

branches.en: a small boat drifting where the wind sends it
branches.cn: 小船随风漂到哪里就是哪里

branches.en: the same spared outcome, given as feeling and as act
branches.cn: 同一种「免于受罚」的结果，一面是心软，一面是行为

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for pay and price, a Latin trading root, and two English suffixes for having and lacking a quality.
intro.cn: 这个词依托一个表示报酬与代价的拉丁名词、一个拉丁交易词根，以及两个表示「有」与「无」某种性质的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: A Latin noun of pay and a trading root stand behind the French word that English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 一个表示报酬的拉丁名词与一个交易词根，支撑着英语借来的法语词形。

definition_zh: 仅仅的；只不过的；纯粹的；十足的；未掺杂的（古义）
definition_en: used to stress that something is no more than what is stated; also, in an older sense, pure and unmixed
core_image: 一杯没有兑水的酒，除此之外什么都没有
scene: 朋友兴冲冲地说起一个计划，其实那只是他昨晚随口想到的一句话。His plan was a mere guess, not a real study.
sceneCN: 这里是「仅仅的、只不过的」（第 1 个义项：强调某物不过如此）；句意为他那个计划只是一个猜测，并不是真正的研究。图中可辨识物件：写满字的草稿纸、咖啡杯。

pos.zh: 仅仅的；只不过的；纯粹的；十足的

derivatives.zh: 由 mere 加 -ly 构成，义为「仅仅；只不过」，常用于修饰动词或整句
由 mere 加 -ness 构成，义为「仅仅是某种东西的状态」，较少使用

senses.title: Nothing more than what is named
senses.definition: used before a noun to stress that the thing is small, simple, or unimportant, and no more than that
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，强调该事物很小、很简单或不重要，不过如此而已
senses.example: The damage was a mere scratch.
senses.exampleCN: 损坏只不过是一道划痕。
senses.why: The Latin source meant pure, with nothing mixed in; from 'nothing added' it was a short step to 'nothing more than', which is how the modern word is used.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词源义为「纯粹的、没有掺入别的」，从「没有添加」到「不过如此」，只差一小步，现代用法正是后者。

senses.title: Sheer and absolute
senses.definition: used to emphasize that a quality is complete and nothing else is involved
senses.definitionCN: 强调某种性质完完全全，别无其他成分
senses.example: We met by mere chance at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站相遇纯属偶然。
senses.why: If mere means unmixed, then mere chance is chance with nothing else behind it, and the word naturally strengthens the noun it modifies.
senses.whyCN: 既然 mere 有「未掺杂」之义，mere chance 就是背后别无其他的偶然，这个词自然会给它所修饰的名词加上分量。

senses.title: Pure and unmixed (archaic)
senses.definition: in older use, describing a substance that has nothing added to it
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的用法中，形容某物质没有掺入任何别的东西
senses.example: The old recipe called for mere wine, with no water added.
senses.exampleCN: 那份旧食谱要求用纯酒，不兑水。
senses.why: This is the original physical sense: a liquid that is itself alone, and the modern 'only' sense is the same idea moved from wine to ideas.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的物质义：一种只由自己构成的液体；现代的「只不过」义，就是把同一想法从酒搬到了观念上。

intro.en: Mere as 'only' and mere as 'lake' are two different words that happen to share a spelling; the adjective came from Latin by way of French.
intro.cn: 表示「只不过」的 mere 和表示「湖」的 mere 是两个碰巧同形的词；形容词这一支经法语来自拉丁语。

items.en: Merus meant pure and unmixed, and it was used of wine that had no water in it.
items.cn: merus 意为纯粹的、未掺杂的，常用来形容不兑水的酒。

items.en: The neuter noun merum named unmixed wine itself, a small but vivid trace of the original sense.
items.cn: 中性名词 merum 直接指未兑水的酒，是原义留下的一个小而生动的痕迹。

items.en: Old French mier or mer meant pure and simple, and English borrowed it in the sense of unmixed.
items.cn: 古法语 mier 或 mer 意为纯粹、单纯，英语借入时取「未掺杂」之义。

items.en: Middle English used mere for pure and unmixed things, then weakened it to mean nothing more than.
items.cn: 中古英语用 mere 形容纯粹、未掺杂之物，随后弱化为「不过如此」的意思。

items.en: The lake sense comes from Old English mere, a different word altogether, and it survives mainly in place names.
items.cn: 表示「湖」的义项来自古英语 mere，完全是另一个词，如今主要保留在地名里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that merely resemble the spelling; the near-meaning group collects words that also mean 'nothing more than'.
note.cn: 形近组收只是拼写相像的词；近义组收同样表示「不过如此」的词。

entries.definition: To combine into one; from Latin mergere, to dip, so only the spelling resembles mere.
entries.definitionCN: 合并为一体；来自拉丁语 mergere（浸入），只是拼写与 mere 相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: A quality that deserves praise; from Latin meritum, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 值得称赞的品质；来自拉丁语 meritum，词源不同，仅拼写相近。

entries.definition: Soft wet ground; from Old Norse, a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 松软的湿地；来自古诺尔斯语，词源不同。

entries.definition: Happy and lively; from Old English myrige, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 快乐活泼的；来自古英语 myrige，词源不同。

entries.definition: And no one or nothing else besides.
entries.definitionCN: 除此之外再没有别的。

entries.definition: Merely, with nothing more than that.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅，不过如此。

entries.definition: Complete and nothing else; used to stress a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 十足的、纯粹的；用来强调某种性质。

entries.definition: Complete and absolute, used of bad or surprising things.
entries.definitionCN: 完全的、绝对的，多用于糟糕或令人吃惊的事物。

normalIntro.en: The adjective began as a word for purity and ended as a word for 'nothing more'; a second, unrelated mere still means a lake.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词从「纯粹」出发，最后表示「不过如此」；另有一个毫无关系的 mere，仍然指「湖」。

normal.en: Merus in Latin means unmixed, so mere wine was wine with no water added.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 merus 意为未掺杂的，所以 mere wine 就是不兑水的酒。

normal.en: The step from 'unmixed' to 'nothing more than' is easy: if nothing is added, then there is nothing else.
normal.cn: 从「未掺杂」走到「不过如此」并不难：既然没有添加，也就没有别的了。

normal.en: Merely is mere plus -ly, and it is the adverb you want when you mean 'only', not the adjective before a noun.
normal.cn: merely 是 mere 加 -ly，当你想说「仅仅」而修饰动词时用它，而不是用放在名词前的形容词。

normal.en: The lake mere comes from Old English and survives in names such as Windermere.
normal.cn: 表示「湖」的 mere 来自古英语，保留在 Windermere 这类地名里。

normal.en: Mere words is a common phrase because words alone, with no action, are exactly what mere means.
normal.cn: mere words 是常见搭配，因为只有话、没有行动，正是 mere 所表达的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of wine with nothing poured into it, then move that 'nothing added' idea onto a guess or a scratch.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯什么都没兑进去的酒，再把「没有添加」这个想法挪到一个猜测或一道划痕上。

abstract.en: Mere always shrinks the noun after it: the word itself is a small spotlight aimed at something small.
abstract.cn: mere 总是把它后面的名词缩小：这个词本身就是一盏照向小东西的小聚光灯。

abstract.en: One spelling for 'pure' and 'lake' shows how English lets two unrelated lives share a single coat.
abstract.cn: 「纯粹」与「湖」共用一个拼写，说明英语能让两个毫不相干的身世穿同一件外衣。

examples.en: The damage was a mere scratch.
examples.cn: 损坏只不过是一道划痕。

examples.en: We met by mere chance at the station.
examples.cn: 我们在车站相遇纯属偶然。

examples.en: The old recipe called for mere wine, with no water added.
examples.cn: 那份旧食谱要求用纯酒，不兑水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米儿」——只剩一粒米儿，少得可怜；mere 就是仅仅的。

root: 拉丁语 merus（纯粹的、未掺杂的，尤指不兑水的酒）经古法语 mier 进入英语；另有一个来自古英语 mere 的同形词，意为「湖」，二者无关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is 'nothing added'; it yields the everyday 'nothing more than', the emphatic 'sheer', and the archaic literal 'unmixed'.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「没有添加」；由此得到日常的「不过如此」、加强语气的「十足」，以及古老的字面义「未掺杂」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass of wine with nothing poured into it, pure and alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杯没有兑入任何东西的酒，纯粹而孤立。

branches.en: a scratch too small to matter
branches.cn: 一道小得不必在意的划痕

branches.en: two people meeting by chance at a station
branches.cn: 两个人在车站偶然相遇

branches.en: a glass of wine with no water in it
branches.cn: 一杯没有兑水的酒

branches.en: the same 'nothing else' said of size and of cause
branches.cn: 同一种「别无其他」，一处说大小，一处说原因

branches.en: an old recipe that insists on the pure liquid
branches.cn: 一份坚持要用纯液的旧食谱

intro.en: The adjective rests on a Latin word for purity, its noun for unmixed wine, and an English adverb suffix that turns it into merely.
intro.cn: 这个形容词依托一个表示纯粹的拉丁词、一个指未兑水之酒的名词，以及一个把它变成 merely 的英语副词后缀。

latinIntro.en: A Latin adjective of purity and its noun for unmixed wine lead through French to the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 表示纯粹的拉丁形容词及其指未兑水之酒的名词，经法语通向英语形容词。

definition_zh: 仅仅；只不过；只是
definition_en: only, and nothing more than what is named
core_image: 一只空盒子，打开后里面只有一张写着「仅此而已」的纸条
scene: 面试官强调，这份工作需要的不是天赋而是耐心。The job merely requires patience, not special talent.
sceneCN: 这里指限定范围、排除更多要求（第 1 个义项：仅仅，别无其他）；句意为这份工作只需要耐心，并不需要特殊天赋；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 仅仅；只不过；只是

derivatives.zh: 仅仅的；纯粹的
最微小的（最高级）
纯粹；单纯（较少用）

senses.title: Only and nothing more
senses.definition: used to limit a statement to what is named and exclude anything more
senses.definitionCN: 把陈述限定在所说的内容上，排除更多的东西
senses.example: He is merely a clerk in a large office.
senses.exampleCN: 他只是一家大事务所里的职员。
senses.why: The word draws a boundary around the description and denies any larger claim.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在描述周围画下一道边界，否认任何更大的说法。

senses.title: No more than
senses.definition: used to lower the importance of what follows
senses.definitionCN: 用来降低随后内容的重要性
senses.example: The delay was merely a technical glitch.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误不过是一个技术故障。
senses.why: Here the minimizer deflates significance, telling the listener not to treat the thing as serious.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个「缩小词」给重要性放气，告诉听者不必把此事看得严重。

senses.title: Only a matter of
senses.definition: used before a noun to reduce an issue to one simple factor
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，把问题归结为单一简单因素
senses.example: Success here is merely a question of timing.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里，成功只是时机问题。
senses.why: The pattern collapses a complex situation into one named factor, often for rhetorical effect.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式把复杂情形压缩成单一因素，常带修辞效果。

senses.title: Not merely
senses.definition: in the pattern not merely, used to say something is more than what is named
senses.definitionCN: 在「不只是」的结构中，表示某物超出所说的范围
senses.example: The law is not merely a set of rules but a social institution.
senses.exampleCN: 法律不只是一套规则，而是一种社会制度。
senses.why: Negating the minimizer opens the scale upward; the sentence promises a larger description to come.
senses.whyCN: 否定这个「缩小词」会把尺度向上打开，句子随即承诺一个更大的说法。

senses.title: Merely by doing
senses.definition: used to say that a small action is enough
senses.definitionCN: 表示一个小小的动作就已足够
senses.example: You can sharpen the image merely by changing one setting.
senses.exampleCN: 你只需改动一个设置就能让图像更清晰。
senses.why: The by-phrase presents the minimum sufficient means, with no extra effort implied.
senses.whyCN: 「通过」短语给出最小充分手段，暗示不需要额外努力。

senses.title: Merely because
senses.definition: used to say that a reason is the only one, often to criticize it as insufficient
senses.definitionCN: 表示这是唯一的理由，常含「理由不足」的批评
senses.example: They rejected the plan merely because it came from a newcomer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拒绝这个方案，仅仅因为它是新来的人提出的。
senses.why: The causal phrase usually carries disapproval: a single reason is treated as too thin.
senses.whyCN: 这一因果短语通常带不赞同：单一理由被视为过于单薄。

senses.title: Merely a formality
senses.definition: used of a step that must be done but has no real effect
senses.definitionCN: 指必须完成却没有实际作用的步骤
senses.example: The signature was merely a formality after the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 决定作出后，签字只是走个形式。
senses.why: The fixed phrase marks a procedure kept for appearance, not for function.
senses.whyCN: 这一固定短语指为了外观而保留的程序，而非为了功能。

senses.title: Downplaying in speech
senses.definition: used in conversation to soften a request or defend an intention
senses.definitionCN: 在对话中缓和请求或为自己的意图辩护
senses.example: I was merely asking, not accusing you.
senses.exampleCN: 我只是问问，并不是在指责你。
senses.why: In speech the word protects the speaker from a stronger reading of their act.
senses.whyCN: 在口语中，这个词保护说话者，免得自己的举动被读得过重。

intro.en: Merely comes from the Latin adjective for pure or unmixed, through French and English, plus the adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; the deeper origin of the Latin adjective is uncertain, and the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「纯粹的、未掺杂的」形容词，经法语与英语，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚；拉丁形容词的更早词根难以确证，英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The Latin adjective merus means pure, unmixed or nothing but.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词意为「纯粹的、未掺杂的」，引申为「不过是」。

items.en: Old French mier carries the sense of pure or entire into French.
items.cn: 古法语形容词把「纯粹、完整」的意思带入法语。

items.en: Middle English mere means pure or simple, and the modern sense of only develops from it.
items.cn: 中古英语形容词意为「纯粹的、简单的」，现代「仅仅」义由此发展。

items.en: The adverb merely grows out of the adjective with the usual suffix, first meaning purely and then only.
items.cn: 副词由形容词加常见后缀构成，先表「纯粹地」，再表「仅仅」。

items.en: The English adverb is recorded from the late medieval period; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语副词见于中世纪末期，确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: The deeper root of the Latin adjective cannot be confirmed, and no confident Indo-European source can be named; this uncertainty concerns the root, not the clear Latin origin of the word itself.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词的更早词根难以确证，无法给出有把握的印欧语来源；这属于词根层面的存疑，而词本身的拉丁来源是清楚的。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin pure-root; the second group contrasts limits of scope with measures of small size.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「纯粹」词根；第二组对照「限定范围」与「衡量幅度小」。

entries.definition: Nothing more than; also, pure and unmixed in older use.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅、不过是；旧义也指纯粹、未掺杂的。

entries.definition: The superlative of mere, meaning the slightest or smallest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词的最高级，意为最微小的。

entries.definition: The quality of being pure or nothing but; rare.
entries.definitionCN: 纯粹或「仅是」的性质；少见。

entries.definition: Showy but cheap and false; it shares the letters mer- but not the pure-root.
entries.definitionCN: 华而不实、虚有其表的；只共享开头字母，并非同一词根。

entries.definition: No one or nothing else besides the one named.
entries.definitionCN: 除所说的人或物之外再无其他。

entries.definition: Simply, with no more than the named thing; also used for emphasis in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅，没有更多；口语中也用于加强语气。

entries.definition: In a plain way, without complication; sometimes close to merely.
entries.definitionCN: 以简单、不加复杂化的方式；有时接近「只不过」。

entries.definition: A phrase that explicitly denies any larger claim.
entries.definitionCN: 明示否认任何更大说法的短语。

entries.definition: Only just, in terms of quantity or degree, not scope.
entries.definitionCN: 就数量或程度而言「刚刚够」，不是限定范围。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pure-root, the real limiting patterns and the real speech use for softening.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「纯粹」词根、真实的限定句式，以及口语中缓和语气的真实用法。

normal.en: The root means pure or unmixed, so merely strips a statement down to one item.
normal.cn: 词根意为「纯粹、未掺杂」，所以这个词把一句话削到只剩一项。

normal.en: Not merely is the door that opens upward: there is always more to say.
normal.cn: 「不只是」是一扇向上的门：后面总有更多话要说。

normal.en: Merely by changing one setting shows how small the sufficient action can be.
normal.cn: 「只需改一个设置」说明充分行动可以多小。

normal.en: Merely because usually sounds like a complaint about a thin reason.
normal.cn: 「仅仅因为」听上去通常是在抱怨理由太薄。

normal.en: In an argument, merely asking is a shield, not a question.
normal.cn: 在争执中，「只是问问」是一面盾牌，而不是一个问题。

abstract.en: Limiting a thing to its name is a way of refusing to let it grow.
abstract.cn: 把事物限定在它的名称上，就是拒绝让它长大。

abstract.en: The word is small but it draws a hard line around a whole claim.
abstract.cn: 这个词很短，却在整段断言周围画出硬线。

abstract.en: Saying merely is often a way to be modest and firm at the same time.
abstract.cn: 说「仅仅」，常常是既谦逊又坚定。

examples.en: The change was merely cosmetic and fooled no one.
examples.cn: 这个改动只是表面功夫，骗不了任何人。

examples.en: She was not merely tired; she was ill.
examples.cn: 她不只是累了，而是病了。

examples.en: The fee is merely a formality to cover paperwork.
examples.cn: 这笔费用只是覆盖文书工作的形式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「秘而利」——秘密很小，仅此而已

root: 拉丁语形容词「纯粹的、未掺杂的」经古法语与中古英语进入英语，先表「纯粹」，再发展出「仅仅」；副词由该形容词加后缀构成。直接拉丁来源清楚，但其更早词根难以确证，英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate bare limitation, lowered importance, a single-factor reduction, the not-merely expansion, minimum means, a thin reason, an empty formality and polite downplaying.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理纯粹的限定、降低重要性、归结为单一因素、「不只是」的扩展、最小手段、单薄理由、空洞形式，以及礼貌淡化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty box that contains only a slip reading nothing more.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只空盒子，里面只有一张写着「仅此而已」的纸条。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: the statement stops at what is named.
branches.cn: 边界：陈述停在所说的内容上。

branches.en: THE DEFLATION: lowering importance and reducing an issue to one factor.
branches.cn: 放气：降低重要性，把问题压成单一因素。

branches.en: THE OPEN SCALE: not merely promises something larger beyond the name.
branches.cn: 打开的尺度：「不只是」承诺名称之外还有更大内容。

branches.en: THE THIN SUFFICIENCY: the smallest means and the weakest reason.
branches.cn: 单薄的充分性：最小手段与最弱理由。

branches.en: THE EMPTY SHELL: a formality without effect and a polite shield in speech.
branches.cn: 空壳：无实效的形式与口语中的礼貌盾牌。

intro.en: Merely is a Latin pure-adjective, a French layer and an English adverb suffix; the deeper root of the Latin adjective is genuinely uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「纯粹」形容词、法语层与英语副词后缀构成；拉丁形容词的更早词根确实存疑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin adjective for unmixed supplies the whole family, and its deeper origin cannot be traced with confidence.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「未掺杂」形容词提供整个词族，其更早来源无法有把握地追溯。

items.example: The adjective describes wine with nothing added.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述没有掺入别物的酒。

items.example: The noun shows how concrete the image of purity first was.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词说明「纯」最初有多具体。

items.example: A related adjective keeps the same physical sense.
items.exampleCN: 一个相关形容词保留同样的具体含义。

items.example: French carries the sense forward before English borrows it.
items.exampleCN: 法语在英语借入前把这一含义传下去。

items.example: English shifts from purity to bare limitation.
items.exampleCN: 英语从「纯粹」转向「仅仅」这一限定义。

items.example: The superlative survives in phrases about the smallest trace.
items.exampleCN: 最高级仍保存在表示「最细微痕迹」的短语里。

items.example: The rare noun names the quality of being nothing more.
items.exampleCN: 这个少见名词命名「别无其他」的性质。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a limiter adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成限定副词。

items.example: The adverb is the form that limits a whole statement.
items.exampleCN: 副词形式用来限定整句陈述。
