definition_zh: 优点；长处；价值；功绩；值得
definition_en: a good quality that deserves praise; the real worth of something; a record of service that earns reward; and as a verb, to deserve something
core_image: 桌上摊着一份朴素的工作记录，密密麻麻的小字压过了封面上那个显赫的姓氏
scene: 评审室里只摆着几份匿名材料，桌上没有名片，也没有介绍人，评委们一页页翻过去，在纸边写下批注。The panel chose the plainest proposal on merit alone.
sceneCN: 这里是「优点、真才实学」（第 1 个义项：值得称赞的长处）；句意为评审只凭方案自身的优点，选中了最朴素的那一份。图中可辨识物件：匿名材料、批注笔迹、空着的名片位。

pos.zh: 优点；长处；价值；功绩
值得；应得

derivatives.zh: 由 merit 加 -orious 构成，义为「值得称赞的；有功绩的」
由 merit 与 -cracy（统治）复合而成，义为「精英治理；唯才是举的制度」
由 de-（减损）加 merit 构成，义为「缺点；过失」
由 merit 加 -ed 构成，义为「应得的；理所应当的」

senses.title: A good quality that deserves praise
senses.definition: a quality or feature of a person or thing that is good and deserves to be praised
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物身上值得称赞的好品质、好特点
senses.example: The plan's main merit is that it costs almost nothing to run.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案最大的优点几乎不花钱就能运转。
senses.why: Latin meritum named what a person had earned, so the first sense of the word is the good thing in someone that makes praise seem earned rather than given.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 meritum 指一个人挣得、应得的东西，所以这个词的第一层含义就是人身上那处让人不得不称赞的好处——称赞像是被挣来的，而不是白送的。

senses.title: The real worth of something
senses.definition: the actual worth or value of something, weighed when people judge whether it is any good
senses.definitionCN: 事物本身的实际价值，是人们在判断好坏时所称量的东西
senses.example: The judges compared the merits of the two designs before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 评委在投票前比较了两个设计各自的价值。
senses.why: Once merit means what is deserved, judging a thing on merit means setting aside the label and weighing what it can really do.
senses.whyCN: 既然 merit 指「应得之物」，那么按 merit 评判一事物，就是把招牌放到一边，只称量它真正能做到什么。

senses.title: A record that earns reward or honour
senses.definition: the accumulated record of good service or achievement that makes a person deserve reward, promotion or public honour
senses.definitionCN: 长期积累的良好服务或成绩，使人有资格获得奖赏、晋升或公开表彰
senses.example: Years of quiet merit finally brought her the senior post.
senses.exampleCN: 多年默默积累的功绩终于让她得到了那个高级职位。
senses.why: Because merit is something earned, it can be counted over time, and a long count of good work turns into the sense of service that a medal or a promotion answers.
senses.whyCN: 因为 merit 是挣来的东西，它可以随时间累积；长期积累的好工作就变成「功劳」这一层含义，奖章或晋升正是对它的回应。

senses.title: To deserve something
senses.definition: to be worth something, or to have earned attention, praise, punishment or serious consideration
senses.definitionCN: 够得上某物，或已经挣得注意、称赞、惩罚或认真对待的资格
senses.example: The question merits a careful answer rather than a quick guess.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题值得认真作答，而不该随手猜一句。
senses.why: The verb keeps the oldest Latin meaning almost untouched: merere was to earn, so to merit something is to have already earned it and therefore to deserve it.
senses.whyCN: 动词义几乎原样保留了拉丁语 merere 最古老的意思「挣得」：to merit 某物，就是已经把它挣到手，因此「值得」。

intro.en: Merit goes back to a Latin verb for earning, and the noun for the thing earned passed through French into English, where it became both a quality and a verb of deserving.
intro.cn: merit 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「挣得」的动词，指「挣得之物」的名词经法语进入英语，后来既是优点，也作「值得」的动词。

items.en: Merere meant to earn, to gain by service, and it already carried the idea that pay follows work.
items.cn: merere 意为挣得、靠出力获得，本身已带着「先有付出、后有回报」的意思。

items.en: Meritum was the noun for what had been earned or deserved, whether a wage, a reward or a good name.
items.cn: meritum 是名词，指挣得或应得的东西，可以是工钱、奖赏，也可以是好名声。

items.en: Old French took the Latin noun as merite, meaning worth, value or a deserving act, and used it in both praise and blame.
items.cn: 古法语把这一拉丁名词写作 merite，意为价值、长处或值得称道的行为，褒贬两边都用。

items.en: Middle English merit named a quality worth praising and also the state of being entitled to a reward.
items.cn: 中古英语的 merit 既指值得称赞的品质，也指有资格获得奖赏的状态。

items.en: Modern English added the verb sense of deserving and kept the phrase on merit for judging without favour.
items.cn: 现代英语补上动词「值得」的用法，并保留 on merit 这一说法，指不带偏私地评判。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the Latin earning family, including a prefixed word that reverses the value; the near-meaning group collects words for goodness and worth.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「挣得」词族，其中包括一个把价值反过来、加了前缀的词；近义组收表示良善与价值的词。

entries.definition: Deserving praise because of good work or service.
entries.definitionCN: 因出色的工作或贡献而值得称赞的。

entries.definition: A system in which power belongs to those who have earned it by ability.
entries.definitionCN: 权力归于凭才能挣得位置者的制度。

entries.definition: A fault or failing that counts against a person, the opposite of a merit.
entries.definitionCN: 记在人账上的缺点或过失，与优点相对。

entries.definition: Earned and therefore justly given, as of praise or punishment.
entries.definitionCN: 因挣得而应当给予的，用于称赞或惩罚。

entries.definition: A morally good quality in a person, especially one long practised.
entries.definitionCN: 人身上道德上的好品质，尤指长期养成的。

entries.definition: The true value of a thing, measured apart from its price or label.
entries.definitionCN: 事物真正的价值，不以价钱或标签衡量。

entries.definition: The importance or usefulness that something has for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 某物对某个用途的重要性或用处。

entries.definition: A quality a person or thing is good at, seen as a resource.
entries.definitionCN: 人或事物擅长的那一处品质，被看作可用的资源。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb for earning; the family keeps returning to what is earned, what deserves praise and what can therefore be taken away.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「挣得」的动词上，同族词反复回到挣得之物、值得称赞之处，以及因而已可被拿走的东西。

normal.en: Merere in Latin means to earn, so merit is not a gift but a balance built up by work.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 merere 意为挣得，所以 merit 不是白送的礼，而是靠工作一点点攒出来的余额。

normal.en: Meritum is the thing earned, which is why the English noun can mean both a good quality and a record of service.
normal.cn: meritum 指挣得之物，所以英语名词既能指好品质，也能指功劳记录。

normal.en: Meritorious adds -orious and says a person or an act is full of merit.
normal.cn: meritorious 加 -orious，表示某人或某事充满 merit。

normal.en: Demerit adds de-, which takes value away, so the word names a fault instead of a virtue.
normal.cn: demerit 加 de-，把价值减掉，于是这个词指过失而不是美德。

normal.en: Meritocracy joins merit to -cracy, rule by those who have earned the right to rule.
normal.cn: meritocracy 把 merit 与 -cracy 组合，指由挣得统治资格者来统治。

abstract.en: A word for earned value suggests that praise is not something handed out but something a person has already paid for in effort.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「挣得价值」的词说明：称赞不是随手发的，而是人已经用力气付过账的。

abstract.en: Judging on merit asks a hard question, what would remain of this person if the name and the uniform were removed.
abstract.cn: 按 merit 评判要回答一个难题：若去掉姓名与制服，这个人还剩下什么。

abstract.en: Because merit can be counted and also taken away, the word quietly holds both fairness and the fear of losing it.
abstract.cn: 因为 merit 既能累积也能被扣掉，这个词同时装着公平，以及失去公平的忧虑。

examples.en: The panel judged the entries on merit alone.
examples.cn: 评审只看作品本身的长处。

examples.en: The proposal merits a second reading.
examples.cn: 这项提议值得再读一遍。

examples.en: Her merit was recognized long before the title arrived.
examples.cn: 早在头衔到来之前，她的功劳就已被看见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卖力特」——肯卖力气的人特别值得称赞；记住 merit 是优点、值得。

root: 拉丁语 merere（挣得、应得）派生出 meritum（应得之物），经古法语 merite 进入英语；同族词多与功绩、应得、褒贬有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what has been earned and therefore deserves praise; the senses divide into a good quality, a thing's real worth, a record of service and the verb of deserving.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「挣得因而应得」；义项由此分出值得称赞的长处、事物本身的价值、功劳记录，以及动词「值得」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plain work record lying open on a table, its long column of small entries outweighing the famous name on the cover.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上摊着一份朴素的工作记录，密密麻麻的小字压过了封面上那个显赫的姓氏。

branches.en: a quiet colleague whose steady work everyone trusts
branches.cn: 一位沉默的同事，靠稳定的工作赢得所有人的信任

branches.en: a plain design chosen over a glossy one
branches.cn: 朴素的设计胜过花哨的设计

branches.en: a judge weighing a plan with the price tag turned face down
branches.cn: 评审把价签翻过去，只称量方案本身

branches.en: a long service record read aloud at a ceremony
branches.cn: 典礼上被高声念出的一长串功绩记录

branches.en: a question that makes the whole room go quiet
branches.cn: 一个让全场安静下来的问题

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of earning, its noun for the thing earned, the French form, and English endings that build an adjective, a fault and a system.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示挣得的拉丁动词、指挣得之物的名词、法语形式，以及构成形容词、过失词与制度词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of

definition_zh: 欢乐的；愉快的；喜庆的；微醺的
definition_en: cheerful and full of lively fun; also used of holidays and celebrations to wish joy, and in informal British use, pleasantly drunk
core_image: 壁炉火旺的冬夜，一家人围着桌子唱歌，窗上贴满手剪的雪花
scene: 壁炉里的柴火烧得正旺，窗上贴着手剪的雪花，孩子们正把彩纸环挂上门框。The whole room felt merry as the family sang together.
sceneCN: 这里是「欢乐的、愉快的」（第 1 个义项：心情欢快）；句意为全家人一起唱歌时，整个屋子都显得喜气洋洋。图中可辨识物件：壁炉、纸雪花、彩纸环。

pos.zh: 欢乐的；愉快的；喜庆的；微醺的

derivatives.zh: 由 merry 去 y 加 -ment 构成，义为「欢乐；欢闹」
由 merry 去 y 加 -ly 构成，义为「欢快地；愉快地」
由 merry 与 making 复合而成，义为「欢庆；作乐」

senses.title: Cheerful and full of lively fun
senses.definition: cheerful, happy and full of lively fun, especially when people are together
senses.definitionCN: 高兴、快活、充满热闹的乐趣，尤指与人相处时
senses.example: The children grew merry as the music started.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐一响，孩子们就快活起来。
senses.why: Old English myrige meant pleasing and agreeable, so the earliest sense is not loud laughter but a mood that feels good to be inside.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 myrige 意为「令人愉快的、合意的」，所以最早的意思不是放声大笑，而是一种让人觉得舒服、愿意待在其中的心境。

senses.title: Lively and festive, as of a holiday
senses.definition: used of holidays and celebrations to wish someone joy, as in the fixed greeting for Christmas
senses.definitionCN: 用于节日与庆祝场合，向人道贺，如圣诞节的固定祝语
senses.example: They hung coloured lights and wished every neighbour a merry Christmas.
senses.exampleCN: 他们挂起彩灯，向每位邻居道一声圣诞快乐。
senses.why: Once a feast is a shared good time, the word attaches itself to the day rather than to the feeling, and ends up fixed inside holiday greetings.
senses.whyCN: 当宴饮成了众人共享的好时光，这个词就黏到日子本身上，而不只是心情，最后被固定进节日祝语里。

senses.title: Slightly drunk and cheerful
senses.definition: in informal British use, pleasantly drunk and therefore more talkative and cheerful than usual
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中指喝得恰到好处、因而比平时更爱说笑的状态
senses.example: After two glasses of wine he was merry but still polite.
senses.exampleCN: 两杯酒下肚，他有了些酒意，却仍旧有礼。
senses.why: Drink lowers the guard, so the cheerfulness the word already names turns into the visible, glass-in-hand kind that loosens the tongue.
senses.whyCN: 酒放松了戒备，于是这个词本来就指的欢快，变成一种看得见、手上有杯子、会松开舌头的热闹。

intro.en: Merry belongs to the Germanic side of English and goes back to an Old English adjective meaning pleasing; no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
intro.cn: merry 属于英语中的日耳曼语这一支，可追溯到意为「令人愉快的」的古英语形容词；它没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: A reconstructed adjective meaning agreeable or pleasant lay behind the word; scholars generally link it to a root for short, with the idea of time passing pleasantly.
items.cn: 这个词背后是一个重构的形容词，意为「合意的、令人愉快的」；一般认为它与表示「短」的词根有关，即时光短而愉快。

items.en: Myrige meant pleasing, delightful and agreeable, and it described places, sounds and company as much as people.
items.cn: myrige 意为令人愉快的、可爱的、合意的，既能形容人，也能形容地方、声音与同伴。

items.en: Middle English mery narrowed toward cheerful and lively, and the spelling settled on merry in the north.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mery 收窄为「快活、有生气」，拼写最终在北方定为 merry。

items.en: From the idea of a loosened, cheerful mood came the informal sense of pleasantly drunk, which stayed common in British speech.
items.cn: 从「心情松弛、快活」这一想法，引申出「微醺」的口语义，这个用法在英式英语中一直常见。

items.en: Modern English keeps merry mostly in fixed greetings and set phrases, while everyday cheerfulness is usually carried by other words.
items.cn: 现代英语里 merry 多保留在固定祝语与成语中，日常的「快活」通常由别的词来承担。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the merry family plus one word that only shares the sound; the near-meaning group collects words for cheer, jollity and celebration.
note.cn: 形近组收 merry 的词族，另加一个只是读音相近的词；近义组收表示快活、热闹与喜庆的词。

entries.definition: Lively fun and laughter shared by a group.
entries.definitionCN: 一群人共享的热闹与笑声。

entries.definition: In a cheerful, lively way.
entries.definitionCN: 以欢快、有生气的方式。

entries.definition: The act of celebrating noisily and happily.
entries.definitionCN: 热热闹闹地庆祝的行为。

entries.definition: Only the sound is close; this verb means to become husband and wife, with no shared origin.
entries.definitionCN: 只是读音相近，这个词意为结婚，词源并不相同。

entries.definition: Showing good spirits, often as a steady habit rather than a burst of fun.
entries.definitionCN: 显得心情好，常是稳定的性情，而非一阵热闹。

entries.definition: Full of deep gladness, stronger and more inward than mere high spirits.
entries.definitionCN: 充满深切喜悦，比单纯兴致高更强烈、更内在。

entries.definition: Good-humoured and sociable, often with a hearty, slightly loud manner.
entries.definitionCN: 脾气温和、爱交际，常带爽朗而略响亮的派头。

entries.definition: Belonging to a feast or holiday, marked by decoration and celebration.
entries.definitionCN: 属于节庆的，以装点与庆祝为特征。

normalIntro.en: The word comes from an Old English adjective for what feels agreeable; its family keeps the shared good time, the laughter around it and the greetings it ended up inside.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自一个意为「令人觉得合意」的古英语形容词，同族词保留着共享的好时光、身旁的笑声，以及它最后被装进去的祝语。

normal.en: Myrige in Old English meant pleasing, so merry began as a good feeling rather than as noise.
normal.cn: 古英语 myrige 意为令人愉快，所以 merry 起初是一种好心情，而不是吵闹。

normal.en: The comparative is merrier, not more merry, because the word is short and old enough for the -er ending.
normal.cn: 比较级是 merrier 而不是 more merry，因为这个词又短又古老，够得上用 -er 词尾。

normal.en: Merriment adds -ment and turns the adjective into the shared state of being merry.
normal.cn: merriment 加 -ment，把形容词变成一种共享的「欢闹状态」。

normal.en: Merrily adds -ly, and the doubled r keeps the short e sound of merry.
normal.cn: merrily 加 -ly，双写的 r 保住了 merry 里短促的 e 音。

normal.en: Merry is now locked inside greetings such as Merry Christmas, which outlived most of its free uses.
normal.cn: merry 如今被锁在 Merry Christmas 这类祝语里，而这些祝语比它大多数自由用法活得更久。

abstract.en: A word for a pleasant mood ended up naming a whole season, which shows how a feeling can attach itself to a date on the calendar.
abstract.cn: 一个表示愉快心情的词最后指整个节季，这说明一种感受可以黏到日历上的某个日子上。

abstract.en: Merry lives mostly in greetings now, a reminder that some words survive by being said at the right moment.
abstract.cn: merry 如今多活在祝语里，提醒人有些词是靠「在对的时刻说出来」而存活的。

abstract.en: The same word can mean happy and slightly drunk, because both describe a guard that has been let down.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指快活又能指微醺，因为两者都描述一道被放下的戒备。

examples.en: The room grew merry as the fire caught and the singing began.
examples.cn: 火苗窜起、歌声响起时，屋子里渐渐欢腾起来。

examples.en: They wished the old man a merry Christmas and left a small parcel.
examples.cn: 他们祝老人圣诞快乐，留下一个小包裹。

examples.en: Two cups of hot wine made him merry enough to tell stories.
examples.cn: 两杯热酒下肚，他高兴得讲起了故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「玛丽」——节日里人人喊着玛丽，满街欢腾；记住 merry 是欢乐的。

root: 古英语 myrige（令人愉快的）来自原始日耳曼语重构形式 *murgijaz，一般认为与表示「短」的词根有关，即时光短而愉快；细节仍有不同说法，无可靠拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a mood that feels good to be in; the senses spread to the festive day, the holiday greeting and the loosened cheer that comes with drink.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种待着舒服的好心情；义项扩到喜庆的日子、节日祝语，以及酒意带来的松弛欢快。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fire burning high on a winter night, a family singing round the table, hand-cut snowflakes stuck to the window.
core.cn: 核心意象：冬夜壁炉火旺，一家人围着桌子唱歌，窗上贴满手剪的雪花。

branches.en: children laughing as the music starts
branches.cn: 音乐响起时笑成一团的孩子

branches.en: a table crowded with relatives and warm plates
branches.cn: 围满亲人、摆着热菜的桌子

branches.en: a paper greeting pinned above a door
branches.cn: 门楣上贴着的节日祝语

branches.en: two glasses on a table and a loosened tie
branches.cn: 桌上两只杯子与松开的领带

branches.cn: 祝语与酒意混在一起的聚会

definition_zh: 混乱；脏乱；污物；困境；弄乱；食堂
definition_en: an untidy or dirty state; the waste left behind; a difficult situation; a group of people who eat together or the room where they eat; and as a verb, to make untidy or to spoil
core_image: 聚餐散场后，桌上盘盏堆叠，汤汁洒在桌布上，地上散落着碎屑
scene: 聚餐散场后，桌上的盘子还堆着，地毯上撒了饼干屑，厨房的门半开着。After the dinner party, the kitchen was a complete mess.
sceneCN: 这里是「凌乱、脏乱」（第 1 个义项：东西没归位）；句意为聚餐结束后，厨房一片狼藉。图中可辨识物件：堆着的盘子、地毯上的碎屑、半开的门。

pos.zh: 混乱；脏乱；污物；困境；食堂
弄乱；搞砸

由 messy 去 y 加 -ly 构成，义为「凌乱地」
由 messy 去 y 加 -ness 构成，义为「凌乱；杂乱」

senses.title: An untidy, dirty state
senses.definition: a state in which things are not in order and look dirty or untidy
senses.definitionCN: 东西没有归位、看上去又脏又乱的状态
senses.example: After the dinner party, the kitchen was a complete mess.
senses.exampleCN: 聚餐结束后，厨房一片狼藉。
senses.why: The earliest mess was a portion of food served at table, so the modern sense of disorder still smells of the kitchen: plates, scraps and things left where they fell.
senses.whyCN: 最早的 mess 是端上桌的一份食物，所以今天「凌乱」这一义仍带着厨房气味：盘子、残渣，以及掉在哪里就留在哪里的东西。

senses.title: Dirt or waste left behind
senses.definition: dirty waste matter, especially the droppings of an animal, that somebody has to clean away
senses.definitionCN: 脏的废弃物，尤指动物的粪便，需要有人清理掉
senses.example: Watch the path, the dog leaves a mess on the grass every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 走路当心，那条狗每天早上都在草地上留下一摊脏东西。
senses.why: Once a mess is food that has been served and eaten, what remains on the ground is also a mess, so the word slides from the meal to its leftovers and then to any filth.
senses.whyCN: 既然 mess 是端上桌又被吃掉的食物，留在地上的残渣自然也是 mess，于是词义从饭菜滑向剩渣，再滑向一切脏东西。

senses.title: A difficult or confused situation
senses.definition: a situation full of trouble and confusion, especially one that someone has caused and must get out of
senses.definitionCN: 充满麻烦与混乱的局面，尤指自己造成、又必须脱身的局面
senses.example: He admitted his finances were in a mess after the failed deal.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认那笔交易失败后，自己的财务状况一团糟。
senses.why: When things are physically out of order, affairs can be out of order too, so the untidy room grows into a tangled situation with no easy way out.
senses.whyCN: 当东西在实处乱了套，事情也能乱套，于是凌乱的房间长成一团找不到出口的局面。

senses.title: To make untidy or to spoil
senses.definition: to make something dirty or untidy, or to spoil a plan or arrangement badly
senses.definitionCN: 把东西弄脏弄乱，或把计划、安排彻底毁掉
senses.example: He messed up the schedule by moving two meetings without telling anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他没打招呼就挪动了两个会议，把日程搞乱了。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an act: to put something into a mess, or to ruin it the way a spilled plate ruins a laid table.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：把东西弄成一团乱，或者像打翻一盘菜弄污摆好的桌面那样，把事情毁掉。

senses.title: A group that eats together, or its dining room
senses.definition: a group of people, especially soldiers, who eat together, or the room in which they eat
senses.definitionCN: 一起吃饭的一群人，尤指军人，或他们就餐的房间
senses.example: The officers gathered in the mess before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 军官们在黎明前聚到食堂。
senses.why: The first sense was a portion of food shared at one table; the people who shared it and the room where they shared it then took over the same name.
senses.whyCN: 最初的意思是同桌分享的一份食物；一起分享的人，以及他们分享所在的房间，后来都沿用了这个名字。

intro.en: Mess began as a word for a portion of food sent to table, and it reached English through French from a Latin verb meaning to send.
intro.cn: mess 起初指端上桌的一份食物，经法语进入英语，其源头是拉丁语中表示「送」的动词。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go, and it supplied the verb behind a large family of sending words.
items.cn: mittere 意为送、放出，是这一大批与「送」有关的词共同的动词来源。

items.en: The noun missus named a course of food served at a meal, literally something sent to the table.
items.cn: 名词 missus 指用餐时端上的一道菜，字面意思是「被送到桌上的东西」。

items.en: Old French mes kept the food sense, meaning a portion or a dish, and also a group eating together.
items.cn: 古法语 mes 保留了食物义，指一份或一道菜，也可指一起进餐的一群人。

items.en: Middle English mess first meant a dish of food and a company of diners, especially in a household or an army.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mess 先指一盘食物和一群共餐者，尤用于家庭或军队。

items.en: Modern English pushed the word toward disorder in the eighteenth century, while the dining sense survived in military usage.
items.cn: 现代英语在十八世纪把词义推向「混乱」，而就餐义则在军队用语中保存下来。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same Latin sending root; the near-meaning group collects words for disorder and jumble.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「送」词根上的词；近义组收表示混乱与杂乱的名词。

entries.definition: Untidy, dirty or complicated, said of rooms, hair or situations.
entries.definitionCN: 凌乱的、脏的或复杂的，可用于房间、头发或局面。

entries.definition: A piece of information sent to someone, from the same verb of sending.
entries.definitionCN: 送给某人的一条信息，同出「送」这一动词。

entries.definition: A person who carries a message from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 把消息从一处送到另一处的人。

entries.definition: An object thrown or fired, literally something sent.
entries.definitionCN: 被投出或射出的物体，字面即「被送出的东西」。

entries.definition: A lack of order, often on a larger scale than a messy room.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏秩序，范围常比凌乱的房间更大。

entries.definition: A mass of small things lying about and taking up space.
entries.definitionCN: 散乱堆放着、占地方的一堆小东西。

entries.definition: Complete confusion in which nothing can be controlled.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底失控的混乱。

entries.definition: A confused mixture or a state of muddled thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 混杂的一团，或思路不清的状态。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb of sending; its family keeps returning to food sent to a table, the people around it, and the disorder left when the meal ends.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「送」的动词上，同族词反复回到端上桌的食物、围桌的人，以及餐后留下的凌乱。

normal.en: Mittere in Latin means to send, and missus was a dish sent to the table.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mittere 意为送，missus 就是被送到桌上的一道菜。

normal.en: Old French mes kept the food sense, so English mess first meant a portion or a dish, not a dirty room.
normal.cn: 古法语 mes 保留食物义，所以英语 mess 起初指一份或一道菜，而不是脏屋子。

normal.en: Because diners shared one dish, mess also named the group and the room where they ate, a sense still used in the army.
normal.cn: 因为同桌分食，mess 也指共餐的一群人与他们就餐的房间，这一义在军队中仍在用。

normal.en: Messy adds -y, meaning full of mess, and therefore untidy.
normal.cn: messy 加 -y，意为「充满 mess」，因此是凌乱的。

normal.en: Mess up is the verb phrase that turns the noun into the act of spoiling something.
normal.cn: mess up 这一动词短语把名词变成「把事情毁掉」的动作。

abstract.en: A word that once meant a shared dish now means disorder, which suggests mess is always what a good meal leaves behind.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经指共享菜食的词如今指混乱，这说明混乱往往是一顿好饭留下的残局。

abstract.en: The same word covers the food, the people eating it and the room they sit in, three parts of one ordinary evening.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖了食物、吃饭的人与他们坐的房间，这是一个寻常夜晚的三个部分。

abstract.en: Calling a situation a mess borrows the picture of a table after dinner, because trouble is easier to bear when it looks like crumbs.
abstract.cn: 把局面称作 mess，是借用了餐后桌面的画面，因为麻烦一旦看起来像碎屑，就比较好承受。

examples.en: After the dinner party, the kitchen was a complete mess.
examples.cn: 聚餐结束后，厨房一片狼藉。

examples.en: He messed up the schedule by moving two meetings without telling anyone.
examples.cn: 他没打招呼就挪动了两个会议，把日程搞乱了。

examples.en: The officers gathered in the mess before dawn.
examples.cn: 军官们在黎明前聚到食堂。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是送到共享桌上的一份食物；义项从饭菜扩到残渣，再到凌乱、困境，以及一群人吃饭的房间。

branches.cn: 鞋底在草地上蹭掉脏东西

definition_en: a piece of information sent to someone; the central idea that a speech, book or film wants to convey; a formal official communication; and as a verb, to send a message to someone
core_image: 一块钉在村口的公告板，纸条边角被风吹起，几个人凑近读上面的字
scene: 村口的公告板前围了几个人，纸上写着一行字，边角被风吹得卷起。She read the message twice before walking home.
sceneCN: 这里是「消息、留言」（第 1 个义项：传给别人的信息）；句意为她把那条留言读了两遍才走回家。图中可辨识物件：公告板、纸条、卷起的边角。

pos.zh: 消息；信息；要旨；咨文
发消息；传讯

derivatives.zh: 由 message 的词干加 -er 构成，义为「送信人；信使」
由 message 去 e 加 -ing 构成，义为「消息发送；即时通讯」

senses.title: Information sent to someone
senses.definition: a piece of information, news or a request that one person sends to another
senses.definitionCN: 一个人传给另一个人的一条信息、消息或请求
senses.example: She read the message twice before walking home.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那条留言读了两遍才走回家。
senses.why: Latin mittere meant to send, so a message is literally the thing sent; the word names the content by the act of carrying it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mittere 意为「送」，所以 message 字面上就是「被送出的东西」；这个词是用「传递」这一动作来给内容命名的。

senses.title: The central idea of a speech or work
senses.definition: the main point or lesson that a speech, book, film or advertisement wants its audience to take away
senses.definitionCN: 演讲、书籍、电影或广告希望受众记住的核心观点或教训
senses.example: The message of the film is that small kindnesses travel further than grand promises.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的要旨是：细小的善意比宏大的承诺传得更远。
senses.why: If a message is what is sent, then a work of art also sends something, and the word shifts from the paper to the point the author wants delivered.
senses.whyCN: 既然 message 是被送出的东西，艺术作品也在送出东西，于是词义就从那张纸转到作者想送达的那层意思。

senses.title: A formal official communication
senses.definition: a formal written or spoken statement sent by a government, a leader or an organization to a body or the public
senses.definitionCN: 政府、领导人或组织向机构或公众发出的正式书面或口头说明
senses.example: The president sent a message to Congress on the new budget.
senses.exampleCN: 总统就新预算向国会提交了一份咨文。
senses.why: Because sending is neutral, the same word can serve ceremony as well as chat, and officials borrowed it for statements that must be on record.
senses.whyCN: 因为「送」本身是中性的，同一个词既可服务闲谈也可服务仪式，官方便借它来指必须留档的说明。

senses.title: To send a message to someone
senses.definition: to send a written or electronic message to a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 向某人或某个群体发送书面或电子信息
senses.example: He messaged the whole team as soon as the train stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 火车一停，他就给全队发了消息。
senses.why: Once the noun names the thing sent, it easily becomes a verb: people began to message each other as soon as a channel existed.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词指的是被送出的东西，它就很容易变成动词：一有了传递渠道，人们就开始互相 message。

intro.en: Message comes from the same Latin verb as mission and missile, and it reached English through French as the name for what is sent.
intro.cn: message 与 mission、missile 同出一个拉丁动词，经法语进入英语，本义就是「被送出的东西」。

items.en: Mittere meant to send, to dispatch or to let go, and it stands behind mission, missile and message alike.
items.cn: mittere 意为送、派遣、放出，mission、missile 与 message 都由它而来。

items.en: The participle missus meant sent, and the derived noun named a sending or something dispatched.
items.cn: 分词 missus 意为「送出的」，由它派生的名词指一次发送或被送出之物。

items.en: Medieval Latin missaticum named a message or an errand, literally the business of one who is sent.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 missaticum 指消息或差事，字面是被派出者所办的事。

items.en: Old French message meant news or a communication carried by word or letter, and it entered English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 message 指口头或书信传递的音信，诺曼时期之后进入英语。

items.en: Modern English widened message to the point of a film, then narrowed it again to texts and chats when new channels appeared.
items.cn: 现代英语把 message 扩展到作品的要旨，等到新渠道出现，又把它收回到短信与聊天上。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the Latin sending family; the near-meaning group collects short communications and written notices.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「送」的词族；近义组收简短的通信与书面通知。

entries.definition: A person who carries a message between two places.
entries.definitionCN: 在两地之间传递消息的人。

entries.definition: A formal or humorous word for a letter that is sent.
entries.definitionCN: 对「发出的信件」的正式或戏谑说法。

entries.definition: A portion of food sent to table, later disorder; the same sending verb lies behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 端上桌的一份食物，后来指混乱；背后的动词同样是「送」。

entries.definition: A task or journey given to someone who is sent to do it.
entries.definitionCN: 交给被派出者去完成的差事或行程。

entries.definition: A short written record or a few lines left for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 简短的书面记录，或留给某人的几行字。

entries.definition: A short internal notice sent between members of an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 组织成员之间传阅的简短内部通知。

entries.definition: A written or printed statement that tells people something.
entries.definitionCN: 告知人们某事的书面或印刷说明。

entries.definition: The broader act of passing information, by speech, writing or signal.
entries.definitionCN: 通过说话、书写或信号传递信息的更宽泛行为。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb of sending; its family keeps returning to what is dispatched, who carries it, and the point it is meant to deliver.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「送」的动词上，同族词反复回到被送出之物、送它的人，以及它想送达的那层意思。

normal.en: Mittere in Latin means to send, so a message is the thing that has been sent.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mittere 意为送，所以 message 就是被送出去的那样东西。

normal.en: Missaticum in medieval Latin named an errand or a message, the business of a person who is sent.
normal.cn: 中世纪拉丁语的 missaticum 指差事或消息，即被派出者要办的事。

normal.en: Messenger adds -er to the same stem, naming the person who carries the message.
normal.cn: messenger 在同一词干后加 -er，指送消息的人。

normal.en: Message and mess share the verb mittere, one naming what is sent, the other the dish sent to a table.
normal.cn: message 与 mess 共用 mittere，一个指被送出的东西，一个指送到桌上的菜。

normal.en: Get the message is the idiom built on arrival: the information has reached you and you understand it.
normal.cn: get the message 这一成语建立在「送达」上：信息到了你这里，你也懂了。

abstract.en: A word for a thing sent shows that meaning always needs a carrier, a route and a receiver before it counts as communication.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「被送出之物」的词说明：意思必须先有载体、路线与接收者，才算完成了传递。

abstract.en: The same word covers a note, a film and a presidential address, because all three ask someone to receive something.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖便条、电影与总统咨文，因为三者都在请人接收某样东西。

abstract.en: When the phone lit up, the old noun quietly became a verb, proof that a word changes shape when a new channel appears.
abstract.cn: 手机亮起时，这个古老的名词悄悄变成了动词，证明新渠道出现时词也会改换形态。

examples.en: She read the message twice before walking home.
examples.cn: 她把那条留言读了两遍才走回家。

examples.en: The message of the film is that small kindnesses travel further than grand promises.
examples.cn: 这部电影的要旨是：细小的善意比宏大的承诺传得更远。

examples.en: He messaged the whole team as soon as the train stopped.
examples.cn: 火车一停，他就给全队发了消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妹塞纸」——妹妹把写好的纸条塞进门缝，那就是一条留言；记住 message 是消息。

root: 拉丁语 mittere（送）→ missus（送出的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 missaticum（差事、消息），经古法语 message 进入英语；同族词多与传送、派遣有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something sent from one person to another; the senses divide into a piece of news, the point a work delivers, an official statement and the act of sending.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从一个人送到另一个人的东西；义项分为一条音信、作品要送达的意思、官方说明，以及发送这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board nailed up at the entrance of a village, a paper note flapping at the corner, a few people leaning in to read it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块钉在村口的公告板，纸条边角被风吹起，几个人凑近读上面的字。

branches.en: a note slipped under a door
branches.cn: 塞在门缝下的纸条

branches.en: a clerk handing a sealed letter across a desk
branches.cn: 职员隔着桌子递出封好的信

branches.en: an audience leaving a theatre still arguing
branches.cn: 看完戏仍在争论的观众

branches.en: a speech read aloud in a formal hall
branches.cn: 正式大厅里被朗读的文件

branches.en: a phone lighting up on a pillow
branches.cn: 枕边亮起的手机

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of sending, its participle, the medieval noun for an errand, the French form and two English endings.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「送」的拉丁动词、它的分词、指差事的中世纪名词、法语形式，以及两个英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
